title.en: Volume 130 Biographies 18: Wu Liang, Kang Maocai, Ding Dexing, Geng Bingwen, Guo Ying, Hua Yunlong, Han Zheng, Chou Cheng, Zhang Long, Wu Fu, Hu Hai, Zhang He, Hua Gao, Zhang Quan, He Zhen
title.raw: 卷一百三十 列傳第十八 吳良 康茂才 丁德興 耿炳文 郭英 華雲龍 韓政 仇成 張龍 吳復 胡海 張赫 華高 張銓 何真 Volume 130 Biographies 18: Wu Liang, Kang Maocai, Ding Dexing, Geng Bingwen, Guo Ying, Hua Yunlong, Han Zheng, Chou Cheng, Zhang Long, Wu Fu, Hu Hai, Zhang He, Hua Gao, Zhang Quan, He Zhen

sentences.zh: 吳良，定遠人。

translations.literal: Wu Liang was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Liang came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初名國興，賜名良。

translations.literal: His original name was Guoxing; he was granted the name Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Guoxing, he was given the name Liang by imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 雄偉剛直。

translations.literal: He was imposing and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of imposing stature and uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 與弟禎俱以勇略聞。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Zhen were both renowned for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Zhen were both famed for their bravery and strategic skill.

sentences.zh: 從太祖起濠梁，併為帳前先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor when he rose at Haoliang, and together they served as vanguard before the commander's tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor raised his banner at Haoliang, Wu Liang and his brother both served as vanguard commanders in his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 良能沒水偵探，禎每易服為間諜。

translations.literal: Liang could dive underwater to scout; Zhen often changed clothes to serve as a spy.
translations.idiomatic: Liang could dive underwater on reconnaissance missions, while Zhen often disguised himself to operate as a spy.

sentences.zh: 禎別有傳。

translations.literal: Zhen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 良從取滁、和，戰採石，克太平，下溧水、溧陽，定集慶，功多。

translations.literal: Liang followed in taking Chuzhou and Hezhou, fought at Caishi, captured Taiping, subdued Lishui and Liyang, and secured Jiqing, with many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Liang took part in the capture of Chuzhou and Hezhou, fought at Caishi, seized Taiping, subdued Lishui and Liyang, and helped secure Jiqing, earning many distinctions.

sentences.zh: 又從徐達克鎮江，下常州，進鎮撫，守丹陽。

translations.literal: He again followed Xu Da in capturing Zhenjiang, subduing Changzhou, advancing as pacification commissioner, and garrisoning Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Xu Da in capturing Zhenjiang and Changzhou, was promoted to pacification commissioner, and held Danyang.

sentences.zh: 與趙繼祖等取江陰。

translations.literal: Together with Zhao Jizu and others he took Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhao Jizu and others, he captured Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 張士誠兵據秦望山，良攻奪之，遂克江陰。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng's troops held Qinwang Mountain; Liang attacked and seized it, and thereby captured Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng's forces held Qinwang Mountain, Liang stormed and took it, thereby completing the capture of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 即命為指揮使守之。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed commander to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed garrison commander and charged with its defense.

sentences.zh: 時士誠全據吳，跨淮東、浙西，兵食足。

translations.literal: At that time Shicheng fully held Wu, spanning east of the Huai and west of Zhe, with ample troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Shicheng controlled all of Wu, his territory stretching from east of the Huai to western Zhejiang, and his armies were well supplied.

sentences.zh: 江陰當其要衝，枕大江，扼南北襟喉，士誠數以金帛啖將士，窺釁。

translations.literal: Jiangyin stood at a critical pass, resting on the great river and controlling the throat between north and south; Shicheng repeatedly used gold and silk to entice the officers and men, watching for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin lay on a vital route, fronting the Yangtze and commanding the passage between north and south. Zhang Shicheng repeatedly tried to buy off Liang's officers and men with gold and silk, watching for any chance to strike.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭良曰：「江陰，我東南屏蔽，汝約束士卒，毋外交，毋納逋逃，毋貪小利，毋與爭鋒，惟保境安民而已。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor instructed Liang, saying: "Jiangyin is our southeastern shield. You must restrain your troops: no outside contacts, no harboring fugitives, no grasping for small gains, no seeking decisive clashes—only preserve the borders and keep the people at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor told Liang: "Jiangyin is the shield of our southeast. Keep your men under strict discipline: no dealings with outsiders, no sheltering deserters, no chasing petty gains, and no needless battles—your sole task is to secure the territory and protect the people.

sentences.zh: 良奉命惟謹，備御修飭。

translations.literal: Liang obeyed the order with utmost care and put defenses in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Liang carried out these orders to the letter and kept the defenses in excellent repair.

sentences.zh: 以敗敵功，進樞密院判官。

translations.literal: For his merit in defeating the enemy, he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his victories over the enemy, he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 士誠大舉兵來寇，艨艟蔽江，其將蘇同僉駐君山，指畫進兵。

translations.literal: Shicheng raised a great army to invade; war vessels covered the river, and his general Su Tongqian encamped at Jun Mountain, directing the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng then launched a major invasion; his warships filled the river, and his general Su Tongqian encamped on Jun Mountain to direct the assault.

sentences.zh: 良遣弟禎出北門與戰，而潛遣元帥王子明帥壯士馳出南門。

translations.literal: Liang sent his brother Zhen out the north gate to give battle, while secretly dispatching Marshal Wang Ziming at the head of picked warriors to charge out the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent his brother Zhen out the north gate to engage the enemy, while secretly dispatching Marshal Wang Ziming with a force of picked warriors through the south gate.

sentences.zh: 合擊，大敗之，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: They joined in the attack and inflicted a great defeat, capturing and slaying many.
translations.idiomatic: The two forces converged and routed the enemy, capturing and killing a great number.

sentences.zh: 敵宵遁。

translations.literal: The enemy fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 尋復寇常州，良遣兵從間道殲其援兵於無錫。

translations.literal: Soon they again invaded Changzhou; Liang sent troops by a hidden route and annihilated their relief force at Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: When they soon attacked Changzhou again, Liang sent troops by a hidden route and wiped out their relief column at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 當是時，太祖數自將爭江、楚上流，與陳友諒角，大軍屢出，金陵空虛。

translations.literal: At that time the Founding Emperor often personally led campaigns to contest the upper reaches of the Jiang and Chu regions against Chen Youliang; the main army went out repeatedly, and Jinling was left empty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Founding Emperor was often away in person, fighting Chen Youliang for control of the upper Yangtze, and with the main army repeatedly deployed elsewhere, Jinling stood largely undefended.

sentences.zh: 士誠不敢北出侵尺寸地，以良在江陰為屏蔽也。

translations.literal: Shicheng dared not advance north to seize even an inch of territory, because Liang at Jiangyin served as a shield.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng dared not push north to seize even a foot of ground, for Liang's presence at Jiangyin blocked his path.

sentences.zh: 良仁恕儉約，聲色貨利無所好。

translations.literal: Liang was benevolent, forgiving, frugal, and abstemious, with no fondness for music, women, goods, or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was humane, forgiving, and frugal, with no taste for luxury, pleasure, or gain.

sentences.zh: 夜宿城樓，枕戈達旦。

translations.literal: At night he slept on the city tower, resting on his spear until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He slept on the city walls at night, weapon in hand, until dawn.

sentences.zh: 訓將練兵，常如寇至。

translations.literal: In training officers and drilling troops, he always acted as though invaders were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: In drilling officers and training troops, he always maintained the discipline of imminent battle.

sentences.zh: 暇則延儒生講論經史，新學宮，立社學。

translations.literal: In leisure he invited Confucian scholars to discuss the classics and histories, built a new academy, and established community schools.
translations.idiomatic: In quieter moments he invited scholars to lecture on the classics and histories, built a new academy, and established community schools.

sentences.zh: 大開屯田，均徭省賦。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded military colonies, equalized corvée labor, and reduced taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded military farming, equalized corvée burdens, and lightened taxes.

sentences.zh: 在境十年，封疆宴然。

translations.literal: During ten years in the territory, the borders were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the ten years he held the post, the frontier remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 太祖常召良勞曰：「吳院判保障一方，我無東顧憂，功甚大，車馬珠玉不足旌其勞。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor often summoned Liang to express appreciation, saying: "Vice Director Wu secures this region for us; I have no worry looking eastward. Your merit is very great—carriages, horses, pearls, and jade are insufficient to reward your labors.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor often summoned Liang to express his gratitude, saying: "Vice Director Wu, you have secured this whole region for me, and I need no longer worry about the east. Your service has been immense—carriages, horses, pearls, and jade are not enough to honor it.

sentences.zh: 命學士宋濂等為詩文美之，仍遣還鎮。

translations.literal: He ordered Academician Song Lian and others to compose poetry and prose in praise of him, and sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Academician Song Lian and others to compose poems and essays in his honor, then sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 尋大發兵取淮東，克泰州。

translations.literal: Soon a great force was raised to take eastern Huai and captured Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a major campaign was launched to seize eastern Huai, and Taizhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 士誠兵復出馬馱沙，侵鎮江。

translations.literal: Shicheng's troops again came out at Matuosha and invaded Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's forces again advanced from Matuosha and threatened Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 巨艦數百，溯江而上。

translations.literal: Several hundred great ships sailed upriver.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred large warships sailed up the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 良戒嚴以待。

translations.literal: Liang stood on alert to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang stood the garrison at full alert.

sentences.zh: 太祖親督大軍御之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor personally directed the main army to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor came in person to lead the main army against them.

sentences.zh: 士誠兵遁，追至浮子門。

translations.literal: Shicheng's troops fled, and the pursuit reached Fuzi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's forces fled, and the pursuit carried as far as Fuzi Gate.

sentences.zh: 良出兵夾擊，獲卒二千。

translations.literal: Liang sent troops to attack from both sides and captured two thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent out troops to attack from both flanks and took two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 太祖詣江陰勞軍，周巡壁壘，嘆曰：「良，今之吳起也！」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor went to Jiangyin to reward the troops, toured the fortifications all around, and sighed: "Liang is a Wu Qi of our day!
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor visited Jiangyin to review the troops, inspected the fortifications, and exclaimed: "Liang is the Wu Qi of our age!

sentences.zh: 吳平，加昭勇大將軍、蘇州衛指揮使，移鎮蘇州。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage and commander of the Suzhou Guard, and transferred to garrison Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was promoted to General of Manifest Courage and appointed commander of the Suzhou Guard, with his headquarters moved to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 武備益修，軍民輯睦。

translations.literal: Military preparations were further improved, and soldiers and civilians lived in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He further strengthened the defenses, and army and populace lived in harmony.

sentences.zh: 進都督僉事，移守全州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the chief military commission and transferred to garrison Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the chief military commission and transferred to garrison Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年進都督同知，封江陰侯，食祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangyin with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Hongwu reign he was promoted to assistant commissioner-in-chief, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangyin with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 四年討靖州、綏寧諸蠻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against the barbarians of Jingzhou, Suining, and other regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he campaigned against the tribal peoples of Jingzhou, Suining, and neighboring areas.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣西蠻叛，副征南將軍鄧愈帥平章李伯升出靖州討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Guangxi barbarians rebelled; as deputy to the southern expeditionary general Deng Yu, he led Pacification Commissioner Li Bosheng out from Jingzhou to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the tribes of Guangxi rose in revolt, he served as deputy to the southern expeditionary general Deng Yu and marched from Jingzhou with Pacification Commissioner Li Bosheng to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 數月，盡平左右兩江及五溪之地，移兵入銅鼓、五開，收潭溪，開太平，殲清洞、崖山之眾於銅關鐵寨。

translations.literal: Within several months they fully pacified the lands of the Left and Right Rivers and the Five Streams, moved troops into Tonggu and Wukai, recovered Tanxi, opened Taiping, and annihilated the forces of Qingdong and Yashan at Tongguan and Tiezhai.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months they had pacified the territories of the Left and Right Rivers and the Five Streams, then pushed into Tonggu and Wukai, recovered Tanxi, opened Taiping, and destroyed the forces of Qingdong and Yashan at Tongguan and Tiezhai.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻皆震懾，內附，粵西遂平。

translations.literal: All the barbarians were awed and submitted inwardly, and western Guangdong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples were awed into submission, and western Guangdong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 八年督田鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he supervised farming at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he oversaw agricultural colonies at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，齊王封青州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Prince of Qi was enfeoffed at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Prince of Qi was granted his fief at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王妃，良女也，遂命良往建王府。

translations.literal: The princess consort was Liang's daughter, so he was ordered to go and build the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's consort was Liang's daughter, and he was therefore ordered to Qingzhou to build the princely residence.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒於青，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died at Qing, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died at Qingzhou, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈江國公，諡襄烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Jiang, with the posthumous name Xianglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Jiang, with the posthumous name Xianglie.

sentences.zh: 康茂才

translations.literal: Kang Maocai
translations.idiomatic: Kang Maocai

sentences.zh: 康茂才，字壽卿，蘄人。

translations.literal: Kang Maocai, styled Shouqing, was a native of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Maocai, whose style was Shouqing, came from Qi.

sentences.zh: 通經史大義。

translations.literal: He mastered the great principles of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in the essential teachings of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 事母孝。

translations.literal: He was filial in serving his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted in his care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 元末寇亂陷蘄，結義兵保鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, when bandit turmoil seized Qi, he gathered a volunteer force to protect his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit armies overran Qi in the final years of the Yuan, he raised a local militia to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 立功，自長官累遷淮西宣慰司、都元帥。

translations.literal: For his achievements he rose from district magistrate through successive promotions to Huaidong Pacification Commission and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he rose from district magistrate through successive promotions to commissioner of the Huaidong Pacification Commission and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 太祖既渡江，將士家屬留和州。

translations.literal: After the Founding Emperor had crossed the river, the officers' and soldiers' families remained at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangtze, the families of his officers and soldiers were left at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 時茂才移戍採石，扼江渡。

translations.literal: At that time Maocai shifted his garrison to Caishi, blocking the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Maocai moved his garrison to Caishi to block the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣兵數攻之，茂才力守。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent troops to attack several times; Maocai defended resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent troops against him repeatedly, but Maocai held firm.

sentences.zh: 常遇春設伏殲其精銳。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun set an ambush and annihilated his elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun laid an ambush and wiped out his crack troops.

sentences.zh: 茂才復立寨天寧洲，又破之。

translations.literal: Maocai re-established a camp at Tianning Isle, and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai rebuilt his camp on Tianning Isle, only to be defeated again.

sentences.zh: 奔集慶，太祖克集慶，乃帥所部兵降。

translations.literal: He fled to Jiqing; when the Founding Emperor captured Jiqing, he led his troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Jiqing, and when the Founding Emperor took the city, he surrendered with his forces.

sentences.zh: 太祖釋之，命統所部從征。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor released him and ordered him to lead his troops on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor spared him and ordered him to lead his former troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年授秦淮翼水軍元帥，守龍灣。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed marshal of the Qinhuai Wing Navy and garrisoned Longwan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed marshal of the Qinhuai Wing Navy and posted to garrison Longwan.

sentences.zh: 取江陰馬馱沙，敗張士誠兵，獲其樓船。

translations.literal: He took Matuosha at Jiangyin, defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops, and captured his tower ships.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Matuosha near Jiangyin, defeated Zhang Shicheng's forces, and captured his tower ships.

sentences.zh: 從廖永安攻池州，取樅陽。

translations.literal: He followed Liao Yong'an in attacking Chizhou and took Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liao Yong'an in the attack on Chizhou and captured Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖以軍興，民失農業，命茂才為都水營田使，仍兼帳前總制親兵左副指揮使。

translations.literal: Because military campaigns had caused the people to abandon agriculture, the Founding Emperor appointed Maocai director of waterworks and military colonies, while retaining his concurrent post as left vice commander of the personal guard under the commander's tent.
translations.idiomatic: Because the wars had disrupted farming, the Founding Emperor appointed Maocai director of waterworks and military colonies, while retaining his concurrent post as left vice commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒既陷太平，謀約張士誠合攻應天。

translations.literal: After Chen Youliang had captured Taiping, he plotted to join with Zhang Shicheng in a combined attack on Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Youliang captured Taiping, he planned to join Zhang Shicheng in a combined assault on Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲其速來，破之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor wished him to come quickly so he could be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor wanted him to come quickly so that he could be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 知茂才與友諒有舊，命遣僕持書，紿為內應。

translations.literal: Knowing that Maocai had old ties with Youliang, he ordered a servant sent with a letter, feigning to serve as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Maocai had old ties with Youliang, he had a servant deliver a letter falsely offering to act as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 友諒大喜，問：「康公安在？」

translations.literal: Youliang was greatly pleased and asked: "Where is Lord Kang?
translations.idiomatic: Youliang was delighted and asked: "Where is Lord Kang?

sentences.zh: 曰：「守江東木橋。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "Guarding the wooden bridge east of the river."
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: "He is holding the wooden bridge east of the river."

sentences.zh: 使歸，太祖易橋以石。

translations.literal: When the messenger returned, the Founding Emperor replaced the bridge with stone.
translations.idiomatic: Once the messenger had returned, the Founding Emperor replaced the wooden bridge with a stone one.

sentences.zh: 友諒至，見橋，愕然，連呼「老康」，莫應。

translations.literal: When Youliang arrived and saw the bridge, he was startled and repeatedly called out "Old Kang," but no one answered.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang arrived and saw the bridge, he was stunned and called out repeatedly for "Old Kang," but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 退至龍灣，伏兵四起。

translations.literal: As he withdrew to Longwan, ambush troops rose on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew toward Longwan, ambush troops sprang up on every side.

sentences.zh: 茂才合諸將奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Maocai joined the generals in fierce attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai joined the other generals in a fierce assault and routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉茂才功，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor praised Maocai's achievement and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor praised Maocai's service and rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖親征友諒，茂才以舟師從克安慶，破江州，友諒西遁。

translations.literal: The next year the Founding Emperor personally campaigned against Youliang; Maocai followed with the fleet, captured Anqing, broke Jiangzhou, and Youliang fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Founding Emperor led a personal campaign against Youliang; Maocai accompanied him with the fleet, helped capture Anqing and break Jiangzhou, and drove Youliang west in flight.

sentences.zh: 遂下蘄州、興國、漢陽。

translations.literal: They then subdued Qizhou, Xingguo, and Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Qizhou, Xingguo, and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 沿流克黃梅寨，取瑞昌，敗友諒八指揮，降士卒二萬人。

translations.literal: Moving downstream they captured Huangmei Stockade, took Ruichang, defeated Youliang's Eight Commanders, and accepted the surrender of twenty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Moving downstream they captured Huangmei Stockade and Ruichang, defeated Youliang's Eight Commanders, and accepted the surrender of twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 遷帳前親兵副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 攻左君弼廬州，未下。

translations.literal: He attacked Zuo Junbi at Luzhou, but it was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Luzhou, held by Zuo Junbi, but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 從援南昌，戰彭蠡，友諒敗死。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Nanchang, fought at Poyang Lake, and Youliang was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Nanchang, fought at Lake Poyang, and Youliang was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 從征武昌，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Wuchang, with merit in every action.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Wuchang and distinguished himself throughout.

sentences.zh: 進金吾侍衛親軍都護。

translations.literal: He was promoted to protector of the Golden Guard Personal Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to protector of the Golden Guard Personal Army.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍徐達再攻廬州，克之，取江陵及湖南諸路。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Xu Da in a renewed attack on Luzhou, captured it, and took Jiangling and the routes of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Xu Da in a renewed assault on Luzhou, took the city, and then captured Jiangling and the routes of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 改神武衛指揮使，進大都督府副使。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as commander of the Shenwu Guard and promoted to vice director of the chief military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as commander of the Shenwu Guard and promoted to vice director of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 士誠攻江陰，太祖自將擊之。

translations.literal: Shicheng attacked Jiangyin; the Founding Emperor personally led troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng attacked Jiangyin, the Founding Emperor led troops against him in person.

sentences.zh: 比至鎮江，士誠已焚瓜洲遁。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Zhenjiang, Shicheng had already burned Guazhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Zhenjiang, Zhang Shicheng had already burned Guazhou and fled.

sentences.zh: 茂才追北至浮子門。

translations.literal: Maocai pursued north as far as Fuzi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai pursued north as far as Fuzi Gate.

sentences.zh: 吳軍遮海口，乘潮來薄。

translations.literal: Wu troops blocked the river mouth and, riding the tide, came close to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wu forces blocked the river mouth and, riding the tide, pressed in to attack.

sentences.zh: 茂才力戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Maocai fought fiercely and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai fought fiercely and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 搗淮安馬騾港，拔其水寨，淮安平。

translations.literal: He struck Maluo Harbor at Huai'an, captured its water fort, and Huai'an was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Maluo Harbor at Huai'an, captured the water fort, and pacified the city.

sentences.zh: 尋拔湖州，進逼平江。

translations.literal: Soon he captured Huzhou and advanced to press Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon captured Huzhou and advanced to threaten Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣銳卒迎斗，大戰尹山橋。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent crack troops to meet in battle; a great fight took place at Yinshan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent elite troops to meet them, and a major battle was fought at Yinshan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 茂才持大戟督戰，盡覆敵眾。

translations.literal: Maocai wielded a great halberd to direct the battle and completely overthrew the enemy force.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai fought at the front with a great halberd and completely destroyed the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 與諸將合圍其城，軍齊門。

translations.literal: Together with the other generals he completed the encirclement of the city, encamping at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the other generals he completed the encirclement of the city, encamping at Qimen Gate.

sentences.zh: 平江下，還取無錫。

translations.literal: After Pingjiang fell, he returned and took Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Pingjiang fell, he returned and captured Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 遷同知大都督府事兼太子右率府使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the chief military commission and concurrently made director of the crown prince's right guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the chief military commission and concurrently appointed director of the crown prince's right guard.

sentences.zh: 子鐸，年十歲，入侍皇太子讀書大本堂。

translations.literal: His son Duo, aged ten, entered service to attend the crown prince in study at the Hall of Great Principles.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duo, aged ten, entered the Hall of Great Principles to attend the crown prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 以父功封蘄春侯，食祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: For his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qichun with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: For his father's service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qichun with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 督民墾田鳳陽。

translations.literal: He supervised the people in opening farmland at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the reclamation of farmland at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 帥兵征辰州蠻，平施、疊諸州。

translations.literal: He led troops to campaign against the Chenzhou barbarians and pacified the prefectures of Shi, Die, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops against the tribal peoples of Chenzhou and pacified the prefectures of Shi, Die, and others.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍達北征。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Da on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand General Xu Da on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 又從征南將軍傅友德征雲南，克普定，破華楚山諸寨。

translations.literal: He again followed the southern expeditionary general Fu Youde in campaigning against Yunnan, captured Puding, and broke the stockades of Huachu Mountain and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed the southern expeditionary general Fu Youde into Yunnan, captured Puding, and destroyed the stockades around Huachu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 卒於軍，年二十三。

translations.literal: He died in the army, aged twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died on campaign, aged twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 追封蘄國公，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Qi, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Qi, with the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 子淵幼未襲，授散騎舍人。

translations.literal: His son Yuan was young and had not yet inherited the title; he was appointed attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan was still too young to inherit the title and was appointed attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事革冠服，勒居山西，遂不得嗣。

translations.literal: Later, for an offense he was stripped of cap and robes and compelled to reside in Shanxi, and thus could not succeed to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was punished for an offense, stripped of his rank and compelled to live in Shanxi, and thus never inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弘治末，錄茂才後為世襲千戶。

translations.literal: At the end of the Hongzhi reign, Maocai's descendants were recorded and granted hereditary command of a thousand-household unit.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongzhi reign, Maocai's descendants were recognized and granted a hereditary command of a thousand-household unit.

sentences.zh: 丁德興

translations.literal: Ding Dexing
translations.idiomatic: Ding Dexing

sentences.zh: 丁德興，定遠人。

translations.literal: Ding Dexing was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Dexing came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖於濠。

translations.literal: He submitted to the Founding Emperor at Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Founding Emperor at Hao.

sentences.zh: 偉其狀貌，以「黑丁」呼之。

translations.literal: Impressed by his imposing appearance, they called him "Black Ding."
translations.idiomatic: Struck by his imposing appearance, they nicknamed him "Black Ding."

sentences.zh: 從取洪山寨，以百騎破賊數千，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Hongshan Stockade; with a hundred horsemen he broke several thousand bandits and fully accepted their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Hongshan Stockade, where with a hundred horsemen he routed several thousand bandits and accepted their full surrender.

sentences.zh: 從克滁、和，敗青山盜。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Chuzhou and Hezhou and defeated the bandits of Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Chuzhou and Hezhou and defeated the bandits of Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，拔採石，取太平，分兵取溧水、溧陽，皆先登。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, seized Caishi, took Taiping, and with divided forces captured Lishui and Liyang, being first to scale the walls in each case.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with the army, seized Caishi and Taiping, and with detached forces took Lishui and Liyang, being first over the walls in every assault.

sentences.zh: 從破蠻子海牙水寨，搗方山營，擒陳兆先，下集慶，取鎮江。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Manzi Haiya's water fort, stormed the camp at Fang Mountain, captured Chen Zhaoxian, subdued Jiqing, and took Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped break Manzi Haiya's water fort, stormed the camp at Fang Mountain, captured Chen Zhaoxian, took Jiqing, and captured Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 以功進管軍總管。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the army.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 下金壇、廣德、寧國。

translations.literal: He subdued Jintan, Guangde, and Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Jintan, Guangde, and Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 從平常州。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢左翼元帥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to marshal of the left wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to marshal of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 寧國復叛，從胡大海復之。

translations.literal: When Ningguo rebelled again, he followed Hu Dahai in recovering it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningguo rose in revolt again, he followed Hu Dahai in retaking it.

sentences.zh: 分兵下江陰，取徽州、石埭、池州、樅陽，攻江州，移兵擊安慶。

translations.literal: With divided forces he subdued Jiangyin, took Huizhou, Shizhi, Chizhou, and Zongyang, attacked Jiangzhou, and shifted troops to strike Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: With detached forces he took Jiangyin, Huizhou, Shizhi, Chizhou, and Zongyang, attacked Jiangzhou, and then shifted his troops to strike Anqing.

sentences.zh: 所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched he was victorious.

sentences.zh: 復援江陰，略江西傍近州縣，攻雙刀趙，挫其鋒。

translations.literal: He again relieved Jiangyin, overran neighboring prefectures and counties of Jiangxi, attacked Double-Saber Zhao, and blunted his momentum.
translations.idiomatic: He again relieved Jiangyin, raided neighboring prefectures and counties in Jiangxi, attacked the bandit leader Double-Saber Zhao, and blunted his advance.

sentences.zh: 時徐達、邵榮攻宜興，久不下，太祖遣使謂曰：「宜興城西通太湖口，士誠餉道所由，斷其餉則必破。」

translations.literal: At that time Xu Da and Shao Rong were attacking Yixing but had long failed to take it; the Founding Emperor sent a messenger saying: "West of Yixing city lies the outlet to Lake Tai, the route by which Shicheng's supplies pass; cut off his supplies and it will surely fall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Da and Shao Rong were besieging Yixing without success. The Founding Emperor sent word: "West of Yixing lies the outlet to Lake Tai, the route by which Zhang Shicheng's supplies pass. Cut off his supplies and the city will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 達乃遣德興絕太湖口，而並力急攻，城遂拔。

translations.literal: Xu Da then sent Dexing to block the Lake Tai outlet, and with combined force pressed the attack; the city was thereby taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da then sent Dexing to block the Lake Tai outlet while pressing the assault with full force, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 論功授鳳翔衛指揮使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed commander of the Fengxiang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed commander of the Fengxiang Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武帝曾稱其乃“攻無不克，戰無不勝之虎將也”。

translations.literal: Emperor Hongwu once called him "a tiger general who in attack never failed to conquer and in battle never failed to win."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hongwu once called him "a tiger general who never failed to conquer in attack or to win in battle."

sentences.zh: 耿炳文

translations.literal: Geng Bingwen
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bingwen

sentences.zh: 耿炳文，濠人。

translations.literal: Geng Bingwen was a native of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bingwen came from Hao.

sentences.zh: 父君用，從太祖渡江，積功為管軍總管。

translations.literal: His father Junyong followed the Founding Emperor in crossing the river and through accumulated merit became commander-in-chief of the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Junyong crossed the Yangtze with the Founding Emperor and through accumulated service rose to commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 援宜興，與張士誠兵爭柵，力戰死。

translations.literal: While relieving Yixing he contested palisades with Zhang Shicheng's troops and died fighting fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: While relieving Yixing he fought Zhang Shicheng's troops over the palisades and died in fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 炳文襲職，領其軍。

translations.literal: Bingwen inherited the post and took command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen inherited his father's post and took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 取廣德，進攻長興，敗士誠將趙打虎，獲戰船三百余艘，擒其守將李福安等，遂克長興。

translations.literal: He took Guangde, advanced to attack Changxing, defeated Zhang Shicheng's general Zhao Dahu, captured more than three hundred warships, seized the garrison commanders Li Fu'an and others, and thereby captured Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Guangde, then advanced on Changxing, defeated Zhang Shicheng's general Zhao Dahu, seized more than three hundred warships, captured the garrison commanders Li Fu'an and others, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 長興據太湖口，陸通廣德，與宣、歙接壤，為江、浙門戶。

translations.literal: Changxing stood at the Lake Tai outlet, connected by land with Guangde, bordered Xuancheng and Shezhou, and served as the gateway to Jiang and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Changxing commanded the Lake Tai outlet, was linked by land to Guangde, bordered Xuancheng and Shezhou, and formed the gateway to Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 太祖既得其地，大喜，改為長安州，立永興翼元帥府，以炳文為總兵都元帥，守之。

translations.literal: Once the Founding Emperor had obtained this territory he was greatly pleased; he renamed it Chang'an Prefecture, established the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Headquarters, and appointed Bingwen grand marshal commanding the army to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted to have secured the territory, the Founding Emperor renamed it Chang'an Prefecture, established the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Headquarters, and appointed Bingwen grand marshal to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 溫祥卿者，多智數。

translations.literal: Wen Xiangqing was a man of much resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiangqing was a man of considerable shrewdness.

sentences.zh: 避亂來歸，炳文引入幕府，畫守御計甚悉。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he came to submit; Bingwen brought him into his staff and drew up defensive plans in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the chaos, he came to join Bingwen, who brought him onto his staff and worked out defensive plans in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 張士誠左丞潘元明、元帥嚴再興帥師來爭。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng's left chancellor Pan Yuanming and Marshal Yan Zaixing led troops to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's left chancellor Pan Yuanming and Marshal Yan Zaixing led troops to contest the city.

sentences.zh: 炳文奮擊，大敗去。

translations.literal: Bingwen fought fiercely and inflicted a great defeat; they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen fought fiercely and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 久之，士誠復遣司徒李伯升帥眾十萬，水陸進攻。

translations.literal: After some time Shicheng again sent Minister of Education Li Bosheng at the head of a hundred thousand men to attack by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Zhang Shicheng sent Minister of Education Li Bosheng with a hundred thousand men to attack by land and sea.

sentences.zh: 城中兵七千，太祖患之，命陳德、華高、費聚往援。

translations.literal: The troops in the city numbered seven thousand; the Founding Emperor was troubled and ordered Chen De, Hua Gao, and Fei Ju to go in relief.
translations.idiomatic: With only seven thousand troops in the city, the Founding Emperor was alarmed and ordered Chen De, Hua Gao, and Fei Ju to go to their aid.

sentences.zh: 伯升夜劫營，諸將皆潰。

translations.literal: Bosheng raided the camp by night and all the generals fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Bosheng raided the camp by night and routed the relief force completely.

sentences.zh: 炳文嬰城固守，攻甚急，隨方御之，不解甲者月余。

translations.literal: Bingwen held the city in a tight defense; the attack was very fierce, and he met it at every point, going without removing armor for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen held the city under siege, repelling every assault for more than a month without once removing his armor.

sentences.zh: 常遇春復帥援兵至，伯升棄營遁，追斬五千余人。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun again led relief troops to arrive; Bosheng abandoned his camp and fled, and more than five thousand were pursued and slain.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Yuchun arrived with relief troops, Bosheng abandoned his camp and fled; more than five thousand of his men were pursued and killed.

sentences.zh: 其明年，改永興翼元帥府為永興衛親軍指揮使司，以炳文為使。

translations.literal: The next year the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Headquarters was changed to the Yongxing Guard Personal Army Command, with Bingwen as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Yongxing Wing Marshal's Headquarters was reorganized as the Yongxing Guard Personal Army Command, with Bingwen as its commander.

sentences.zh: 已而士誠大發兵，遣其弟士信復來爭。

translations.literal: Before long Shicheng raised a great army and sent his younger brother Shixin to contest it again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Shicheng mobilized a large force and sent his younger brother Shixin to contest the city again.

sentences.zh: 炳文又敗之，獲其元帥宋興祖。

translations.literal: Bingwen again defeated them and captured their marshal Song Xingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen defeated them again and captured their marshal Song Xingzu.

sentences.zh: 士信憤甚，益兵圍城。

translations.literal: Shixin was greatly enraged and added troops to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shixin reinforced his army and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 炳文與費聚出戰，又大敗之。

translations.literal: Bingwen and Fei Ju went out to give battle and again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen and Fei Ju sallied forth and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 長興為士誠必爭地，炳文拒守凡十年，以寡御眾，大小數十戰，戰無不勝，士誠迄不得逞。

translations.literal: Changxing was territory Shicheng was determined to contest; Bingwen held it in defense for ten years in all, using the few against the many in several dozen battles large and small, never failing to win, and Shicheng never achieved his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Changxing was territory Zhang Shicheng was determined to hold. For ten years Bingwen defended it with inferior numbers, fighting several dozen engagements large and small without a single defeat, and Zhang Shicheng never achieved his aim.

sentences.zh: 大軍伐士誠，炳文將所部克湖州，圍平江。

translations.literal: When the main army campaigned against Shicheng, Bingwen led his troops to capture Huzhou and besiege Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched against Zhang Shicheng, Bingwen led his forces to capture Huzhou and besiege Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 吳平，進大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was promoted to commissioner of the chief military commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, he was promoted to commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 從征中原，克山東沂、嶧諸州。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign into the Central Plains and captured the Shandong prefectures of Yi and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign into the Central Plains and captured the Shandong prefectures of Yi and Yi.

sentences.zh: 下汴梁，徇河南，扈駕北巡。

translations.literal: He subdued Bianliang, swept through Henan, and escorted the imperial carriage on the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: He took Bianliang, swept through Henan, and escorted the emperor on his northern tour.

sentences.zh: 已，又從常遇春取大同，克晉、冀。

translations.literal: Later he again followed Chang Yuchun in taking Datong and capturing Jin and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Chang Yuchun in taking Datong and capturing Shanxi and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍徐達征陝西，走李思齊、張思道，即鎮其地。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Xu Da in campaigning against Shaanxi, drove off Li Siqi and Zhang Sidao, and immediately garrisoned the territory.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Xu Da into Shaanxi, drove off Li Siqi and Zhang Sidao, and was posted to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 浚涇陽洪渠十萬余丈，民賴其利。

translations.literal: He dredged more than a hundred thousand zhang of the Hong Canal at Jingyang, and the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged more than a hundred thousand zhang of the Hong Canal at Jingyang, to the great benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 尋拜秦王左相都督僉事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left chancellor to the Prince of Qin and commissioner of the chief military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed left chancellor to the Prince of Qin and commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，封長興侯，食祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changxing with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Hongwu reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changxing with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從大將軍出塞，破元平章乃兒不花於北黃河。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the grand general beyond the frontier and defeated the Yuan pacification commissioner Na'er Buhua at the Northern Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined the grand general on a campaign beyond the frontier and defeated the Yuan pacification commissioner Na'er Buhua at the Northern Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 十九年從潁國公傅龍德征雲南，討平曲靖蠻。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed Duke of Ying Fu Youde in campaigning against Yunnan and suppressed the Qujing barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he followed Duke of Ying Fu Youde into Yunnan and suppressed the tribal peoples of Qujing.

sentences.zh: 二十一年從永昌侯藍玉北征，至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he followed Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu on the northern expedition as far as Lake Buyur.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he joined Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu on the northern expedition as far as Lake Buyur.

sentences.zh: 二十五年帥兵平陝西徽州妖人之亂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he led troops to pacify the rebellion of sorcerers in Huizhou, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he led troops to suppress the sorcerers' rebellion in Huizhou, Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 三十年以征西將軍擒蜀寇高福興，俘三千人。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, as western expeditionary general, he captured the Shu bandit Gao Fuxing and took three thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, as western expeditionary general, he captured the Sichuan rebel Gao Fuxing and took three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 始，炳文守長興，功最高，太祖榜列功臣，以炳文附大將軍達為一等。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Bingwen garrisoned Changxing, his merit was highest; the Founding Emperor posted a list of meritorious ministers and ranked Bingwen, attached to Grand General Da, in the first class.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingwen held Changxing, his service ranked highest among the founders; the Founding Emperor posted a list of meritorious ministers and placed Bingwen, grouped with Grand General Xu Da, in the first rank.

sentences.zh: 及洪武末年，諸公、侯且盡，存者惟炳文及武定侯郭英二人；

translations.literal: By the end of the Hongwu reign, the dukes and marquises were nearly all gone; only Bingwen and Marquis of Wuding Guo Ying remained;
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Hongwu reign nearly all the founding dukes and marquises were dead; only Bingwen and Marquis of Wuding Guo Ying remained;

sentences.zh: 而炳文以元功宿將，為朝廷所倚重。

translations.literal: and Bingwen, as an original merit-holder and veteran general, was relied upon heavily by the court.
translations.idiomatic: and Bingwen, as a founding veteran of the highest rank, was deeply relied upon by the court.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，燕王兵起。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen, the Prince of Yan raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianwen reign, the Prince of Yan rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝命炳文為大將軍，帥副將軍李堅、寧忠北伐，時年六十有五矣。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Bingwen grand general, leading vice generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong on the northern expedition; he was then sixty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Bingwen grand general and sent him north with vice generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong; he was then sixty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 兵號三十萬，至者惟十三萬。

translations.literal: The army was said to number three hundred thousand, but only one hundred thirty thousand arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The army was said to number three hundred thousand, but only one hundred thirty thousand actually arrived.

sentences.zh: 八月次真定，分營滹沱河南北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he halted at Zhending and divided camps north and south of the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he encamped at Zhending and divided his forces north and south of the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 都督徐凱軍河間，潘忠、楊松駐鄚州，先鋒九千人駐雄縣。

translations.literal: Commissioner-in-chief Xu Kai was at Hejian; Pan Zhong and Yang Song were stationed at Mozhou; nine thousand vanguard troops were at Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner-in-chief Xu Kai was posted at Hejian; Pan Zhong and Yang Song held Mozhou; and nine thousand vanguard troops were stationed at Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 值中秋，不設備，為燕王所襲，九千人皆死。

translations.literal: It happened to be Mid-Autumn Festival; they made no preparations and were raided by the Prince of Yan; all nine thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: It was the Mid-Autumn Festival and they were unprepared; the Prince of Yan raided them and all nine thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 忠等來援，過月漾橋，伏發水中。

translations.literal: Zhong and others came to relieve them; crossing Moon-Wave Bridge, ambush troops sprang up from the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the others came to their relief, but as they crossed Moon-Wave Bridge, ambush troops sprang up from the water.

sentences.zh: 忠、松俱被執，不屈死。

translations.literal: Zhong and Song were both captured and, refusing to submit, died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Song were both captured and, refusing to submit, were put to death.

sentences.zh: 鄚州陷。

translations.literal: Mozhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhou fell.

sentences.zh: 而炳文部將張保者降燕，備告南軍虛實。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Bingwen's subordinate general Zhang Bao surrendered to Yan and fully informed them of the southern army's strength and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Bingwen's subordinate Zhang Bao defected to the Prince of Yan and revealed the full disposition of the southern army.

sentences.zh: 燕王縱保歸，使張雄、鄚敗狀，謂：「北軍且至。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan released Bao to return, had Zhang Xiong report the defeat at Mo, and said: "The northern army is about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan sent Bao back with Zhang Xiong to report the defeat at Mozhou, saying: "The northern army is about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 於是炳文移軍盡渡河，並力當敵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bingwen moved his army entirely across the river to meet the enemy with combined force.
translations.idiomatic: Believing this, Bingwen moved his entire army across the river to confront the enemy with full force.

sentences.zh: 軍甫移，燕兵驟至，循城蹴擊。

translations.literal: The army had barely moved when Yan troops suddenly arrived and, following the city wall, struck in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: His army had barely moved when Yan forces suddenly appeared and struck along the city wall.

sentences.zh: 炳文軍不得成列，敗入城。

translations.literal: Bingwen's army could not form ranks and was defeated, fleeing into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen's troops could not form ranks and were driven back into the city in defeat.

sentences.zh: 爭門，門塞，蹈藉死者不可數計。

translations.literal: They struggled for the gates; the gates were blocked, and those trampled to death were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the scramble for the gates the exits were jammed, and countless men were trampled to death.

sentences.zh: 燕兵遂圍城。

translations.literal: The Yan troops then besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops then besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 炳文眾尚十萬，堅守不出。

translations.literal: Bingwen's force still numbered a hundred thousand; he held firm and did not sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen still had a hundred thousand men and held the city without sallying forth.

sentences.zh: 燕王知炳文老將，未易下，越三日，解圍還。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan knew Bingwen was an old general not easily overcome; after three days he lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Bingwen was a veteran not easily defeated, the Prince of Yan lifted the siege after three days and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 而帝驟聞炳文敗，憂甚。

translations.literal: But the emperor suddenly heard of Bingwen's defeat and was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor suddenly heard of Bingwen's defeat, he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 太常卿黃子澄遂薦李景隆為大將軍，乘傳代炳文。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Ceremonies Huang Zicheng then recommended Li Jinglong as grand general and, traveling by relay post, replaced Bingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Ceremonies Huang Zicheng then recommended Li Jinglong as grand general and sent him by relay post to replace Bingwen.

sentences.zh: 比至軍，燕師已先一日去。

translations.literal: By the time he reached the army, the Yan forces had already departed one day earlier.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the army, the Yan forces had already withdrawn the day before.

sentences.zh: 炳文歸，景隆代將，竟至於敗。

translations.literal: Bingwen returned; Jinglong replaced him in command, and in the end came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen returned home; Jinglong took command in his place and ultimately led the army to ruin.

sentences.zh: 燕王稱帝之明年，刑部尚書鄭賜、都御史陳瑛劾炳文衣服器皿有龍鳳飾，玉帶用紅鞓，僭妄不道。

translations.literal: In the year after the Prince of Yan proclaimed himself emperor, Minister of Justice Zheng Ci and Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying impeached Bingwen, saying his clothing and vessels bore dragon and phoenix ornamentation, his jade belt used red lacings, and he was presumptuous and rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: The year after the Prince of Yan proclaimed himself emperor, Minister of Justice Zheng Ci and Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying impeached Bingwen for wearing clothing and using vessels adorned with dragon and phoenix motifs, for wearing a jade belt with red lacings, and for presumptuous and treasonous conduct.

sentences.zh: 炳文懼，自殺。

translations.literal: Bingwen was afraid and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen, in fear, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 子璿，前軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: His son Xuan was vice commissioner of the vanguard army command.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan served as vice commissioner of the vanguard army command.

sentences.zh: 尚懿文太子長女江都公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Jiangdu, eldest daughter of Crown Prince Yiwen.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Jiangdu, eldest daughter of Crown Prince Yiwen.

sentences.zh: 炳文北伐，璿嘗勸直搗北平。

translations.literal: During Bingwen's northern expedition, Xuan once urged a direct strike at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: During Bingwen's northern expedition, Xuan urged a direct assault on Beiping.

sentences.zh: 炳文受代歸，不復用，璿憤甚。

translations.literal: Bingwen was relieved and returned home, was not employed again, and Xuan was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingwen was relieved of command and sent home, never to be employed again, Xuan was filled with bitter anger.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，杜門稱疾，坐罪死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he shut his doors and claimed illness; convicted of a crime, he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he shut himself indoors, feigning illness, and was convicted and executed.

sentences.zh: 璿弟瓛，後軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Huan was vice commissioner of the rear army command.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Huan served as vice commissioner of the rear army command.

sentences.zh: 與江陰侯吳高、都指揮楊文帥遼東兵圍永平，不克，退保山海關。

translations.literal: Together with Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao and regional commander Yang Wen he led Liaodong troops to besiege Yongping; they did not take it and withdrew to hold Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: With Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao and Regional Commander Yang Wen, he led Liaodong troops to besiege Yongping; failing to capture it, they fell back to defend Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 高被間，徙廣西。

translations.literal: Gao fell victim to alienation and was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao fell prey to slander and was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 文守遼東，瓛數請攻永平以動北平，文不聽。

translations.literal: Wen guarded Liaodong; Huan repeatedly asked to attack Yongping so as to threaten Beiping, but Wen would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wen remained in charge of Liaodong, and Huan repeatedly urged an attack on Yongping to threaten Beiping, but Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 後與弟尚寶司卿瑄，皆坐罪死。

translations.literal: Later he and his younger brother, chief minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, were both convicted and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and his younger brother, who served as chief minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, were both convicted and executed.

sentences.zh: 郭英，鞏昌侯興弟也。

translations.literal: Guo Ying was the younger brother of Marquis of Gongchang Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ying was the younger brother of Marquis of Gongchang Guo Xing.

sentences.zh: 年十八，與興同事太祖。

translations.literal: At eighteen he and Xing together served the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he and his brother Xing entered the Founding Emperor's service together.

sentences.zh: 親信，令值宿帳中，呼為「郭四」。

translations.literal: He was trusted and intimate; the Emperor had him stand night watch in the tent and called him "Guo Four."
translations.idiomatic: Deeply trusted, he was ordered to stand night watch in the imperial tent and was affectionately called "Guo Four."

sentences.zh: 從克滁、和、採石、太平，征陳友諒，戰鄱陽湖，皆與有功。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Chu, He, Caishi, and Taiping, campaigned against Chen Youliang, and fought at Poyang Lake, sharing merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Chu, He, Caishi, and Taiping, in the campaign against Chen Youliang, and in the battle of Poyang Lake, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 從征武昌，陳氏驍將陳同僉持槊突入，太祖呼英殺之，衣以戰袍。

translations.literal: On the expedition against Wuchang, Chen's fierce general Chen Tongqian, wielding a spear, charged in; the Founding Emperor called on Ying to kill him and clothed him with a battle robe.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wuchang, Chen Youliang's fierce general Chen Tongqian burst in wielding a spear; the Founding Emperor called on Ying to kill him and rewarded him with a battle robe.

sentences.zh: 攻岳州，敗其援兵，還克廬州、襄陽。

translations.literal: He attacked Yuezhou, defeated its relief force, and then captured Luzhou and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Yuezhou, routed its relief army, and went on to capture Luzhou and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 授驍騎衛千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed battalion commander of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed battalion commander of the Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 克淮安、濠州、安豐，進指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He captured Huai'an, Haozhou, and Anfeng, and was promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Huai'an, Haozhou, and Anfeng, he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從徐達定中原，又從常遇春攻太原，走擴廓，下興州、大同。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in pacifying the Central Plain, then followed Chang Yuchun in attacking Taiyuan, drove off Köke Temür, and captured Xingzhou and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in pacifying the Central Plain, then served under Chang Yuchun at Taiyuan, drove off Köke Temür, and took Xingzhou and Datong.

sentences.zh: 至沙淨州渡河。

translations.literal: He reached Shajing Prefecture and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Shajing and crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 取西安、鳳翔、鞏昌、慶陽，追敗駕宗哲於亂山，遷本衛指揮副使。

translations.literal: He took Xi'an, Fengxiang, Gongchang, and Qingyang, pursued and defeated Jia Zongzhe at Luanshan, and was transferred to deputy commander of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xi'an, Fengxiang, Gongchang, and Qingyang, pursued and routed Jia Zongzhe at Luanshan, and was promoted to deputy commander of his guard.

sentences.zh: 進克定西，討察罕腦兒。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured Dingxi and campaigned against Chakhan Temür.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to capture Dingxi and campaigned against Chakhan Temür.

sentences.zh: 克登寧州，斬首二千級，進河南都指揮使。

translations.literal: He captured and ascended Ningzhou, took two thousand heads, and was promoted to regional commander of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ningzhou, took two thousand heads, and was promoted to regional commander of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時英女弟為寧妃，英將赴鎮，命妃餞英於第，賜白金二十罌，廄馬二十匹。

translations.literal: At that time Ying's younger sister was Consort Ning; as Ying was about to depart for his post, the consort was ordered to give him a farewell feast at his residence, and he was granted twenty jars of white silver and twenty stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ying's younger sister was Consort Ning; as Ying prepared to take up his command, the consort was ordered to host a farewell feast for him at his residence, and he was granted twenty jars of silver and twenty horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 在鎮綏輯流亡，申明約束，境內大治。

translations.literal: At his post he settled displaced persons, clarified regulations, and the territory was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he resettled refugees, enforced discipline, and brought the region to good order.

sentences.zh: 九年移鎮北平。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to garrison Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to command at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 十三年召還，進前軍都督府僉事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was recalled and promoted to vice commissioner of the vanguard army command.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled to court and promoted to vice commissioner of the vanguard army command.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從潁川侯傅友德征雲南，與陳桓、胡海分道進攻赤水河路。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde in campaigning against Yunnan, and with Chen Huan and Hu Hai advanced by separate routes along the Chishui River road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he followed Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde on the Yunnan campaign, advancing by separate routes along the Chishui River with Chen Huan and Hu Hai.

sentences.zh: 久雨，河水暴漲。

translations.literal: After prolonged rain the river rose violently.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains had swollen the river to flood.

sentences.zh: 英斬木為筏，乘夜濟。

translations.literal: Ying cut timber to make rafts and crossed by night.
translations.idiomatic: Ying felled trees to build rafts and crossed under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 比曉，抵賊營，賊大驚潰。

translations.literal: By dawn he reached the rebel camp; the rebels were greatly alarmed and routed.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn he had reached the rebel camp; the enemy panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 擒烏撒並阿容等。

translations.literal: He captured Wusa, A-Rong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Wusa, A-Rong, and others.

sentences.zh: 攻克曲靖、陸涼、越州、關索嶺、椅子寨。

translations.literal: He attacked and captured Qujing, Luliang, Yuezhou, Guansuo Ridge, and Yizi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed and took Qujing, Luliang, Yuezhou, Guansuo Ridge, and Yizi Stockade.

sentences.zh: 降大理、金齒、廣南，平諸山寨。

translations.literal: He received the surrender of Dali, Jinchi, and Guangnan and pacified the mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Dali, Jinchi, and Guangnan submitted, and the mountain stockades were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十六年復從友德平蒙化、鄧川，濟金沙，取北勝、麗江。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again followed Youde in pacifying Menghua and Dengchuan, crossed the Jinsha River, and took Beisheng and Lijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he again followed Youde to pacify Menghua and Dengchuan, crossed the Jinsha River, and captured Beisheng and Lijiang.

sentences.zh: 前後斬首一萬三千余級，生擒二千余人，收精甲數萬，船千余艘。

translations.literal: Before and after he took more than thirteen thousand heads, captured alive more than two thousand men, seized tens of thousands of fine armor, and over a thousand boats.
translations.idiomatic: In all he took more than thirteen thousand heads, captured over two thousand men alive, seized tens of thousands of suits of fine armor, and more than a thousand boats.

sentences.zh: 十七年論平雲南功，封武定侯，食祿二千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when merit in pacifying Yunnan was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuding with an income of twenty-five hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, for his service in pacifying Yunnan, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuding with an income of twenty-five hundred shi of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 英孝友，通書史，行師有紀律，以忠謹見親於太祖。

translations.literal: Ying was filial and brotherly, versed in books and history, disciplined in leading troops, and was treated with intimacy by the Founding Emperor for his loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was filial and loyal to his kin, well read in history, and disciplined in command; the Founding Emperor held him in special affection for his loyalty and prudence.

sentences.zh: 又以寧妃故，恩寵尤渥，諸功臣莫敢望焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, because of Consort Ning, his favor was especially thick, and none of the meritorious ministers dared compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his ties to Consort Ning, his favor was especially great, and none of the founding ministers could compare.

sentences.zh: 勛桀黠有智數，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: Xun was fierce, cunning, and resourceful, and had considerable knowledge of books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was fierce, shrewd, and clever, with a fair grounding in books and history.

sentences.zh: 正德中，鎮兩廣，入掌三千營。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he garrisoned the Two Guangs and entered to command the Three Thousand Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he commanded the Two Guangs and was appointed to lead the Three Thousand Battalion.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，掌團營。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shizong reign he commanded the regiment battalions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he took command of the regiment battalions.

sentences.zh: 大禮議起，勛知上意，首右張璁，世宗大愛幸之。

translations.literal: When the Great Rites Controversy arose, Xun understood the emperor's intent and was the first to support Zhang Cong on the right; the Jiajing Emperor greatly favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Rites Controversy erupted, Xun divined the emperor's wishes and was first to side with Zhang Cong; the Jiajing Emperor came to favor him deeply.

sentences.zh: 勛怙寵，頗驕恣。

translations.literal: Relying on favor, Xun became rather arrogant and willful.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in imperial favor, Xun grew arrogant and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊一清惡之，因其賕請事覺，罷營務，奪保傅官階。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing hated him; because a bribery petition affair came to light, he was removed from battalion duties and stripped of his guardian-tutor ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing detested him; when a bribery scandal came to light, Xun was removed from battalion command and stripped of his guardian-tutor titles.

sentences.zh: 一清罷，仍總五軍營，董四郊興造。

translations.literal: When Yiqing was dismissed, Xun again commanded the Five Armies Battalions and supervised construction at the four suburban altars.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiqing's dismissal, Xun again took overall command of the Five Armies Battalions and oversaw construction at the four suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 明年督團營。

translations.literal: The next year he supervised the regiment battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of the regiment battalions.

sentences.zh: 十八年兼領後府。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he concurrently headed the rear army command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he also took charge of the rear army command.

sentences.zh: 從幸承天，請以五世祖英侑享太廟。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Chengtian, he requested that his fifth-generation ancestor Ying be granted joint sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial visit to Chengtian, he petitioned that his fifth-generation ancestor Ying be granted joint enshrinement at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 廷臣持不可，侍郎唐胄爭尤力。

translations.literal: Court ministers maintained it could not be done; Vice Minister Tang You argued against it with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers objected strenuously, and Vice Minister Tang You led the opposition.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，英竟得侑享。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen, and Ying in the end received joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed them, and Ying was granted joint enshrinement after all.

sentences.zh: 其明年，獻皇稱宗，入太廟，進勛翊國公，加太師。

translations.literal: The next year the Offered Emperor was styled Zong and entered the Grand Temple; Xun was advanced to Duke Who Supports the State and given the title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Offered Emperor was enshrined as an imperial ancestor in the Grand Temple; Xun was promoted to Duke Who Supports the State and given the title Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 先是，妖人李福達自言能化藥物為金銀。

translations.literal: Earlier, the sorcerer Li Fuda claimed he could transform medicines into gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the sorcerer Li Fuda had claimed he could transmute elixirs into gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 勛與相暱。

translations.literal: Xun was on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was on close terms with him.

sentences.zh: 福達敗，力持其獄，廷臣多得罪者。

translations.literal: When Fuda was ruined, Xun forcefully upheld his case, and many court ministers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuda fell, Xun vigorously defended him, and many court ministers suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 至是復進方士段朝用，雲以其所化金銀為飲食器，可不死。

translations.literal: At this time he again presented the Taoist Duan Chaoyong, saying that vessels made from his transmuted gold and silver could grant immortality.
translations.idiomatic: He now introduced the alchemist Duan Chaoyong, claiming that food and drink taken from vessels of his transmuted gold and silver would grant immortality.

sentences.zh: 帝益以為忠。

translations.literal: The emperor all the more regarded him as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded him as all the more loyal.

sentences.zh: 給事中戚賢劾勛擅作威福，網利虐民諸事。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qi Xian impeached Xun for arrogating authority, netting profit, and oppressing the people, among other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Qi Xian impeached Xun for abusing power, extorting profit, and oppressing the people, among other offenses.

sentences.zh: 李鳳來等復以為言。

translations.literal: Li Fenglai and others again spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fenglai and others raised the matter again.

sentences.zh: 下有司勘，勛京師店舍多至千余區。

translations.literal: The case was referred to the relevant offices for investigation; Xun's shops and houses in the capital amounted to more than a thousand units.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred for investigation, and Xun's shops and houses in the capital were found to number more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 副都御史胡守中又劾勛以族叔郭憲理刑東廠，肆虐無辜。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Hu Shouzhong also impeached Xun for putting his clansman Guo Xian in charge of judicial matters at the Eastern Depot and tyrannizing the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Hu Shouzhong also impeached Xun for placing his clansman Guo Xian in charge of judicial matters at the Eastern Depot and terrorizing the innocent.

sentences.zh: 帝置勿治。

translations.literal: The emperor set the matter aside and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set the charges aside and took no action.

sentences.zh: 會帝用言官言，給勛敕，與兵部尚書王廷相、遂安伯陳譓同清軍役。

translations.literal: When the emperor followed the remonstrating officials' advice, he issued an edict to Xun, ordering him together with Minister of War Wang Tingxiang and Earl of Suian Chen Kui to clear up military corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heeded the remonstrators, he issued an edict to Xun, Wang Tingxiang as Minister of War, and Earl of Suian Chen Kui to reform military corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 敕具，勛不領。

translations.literal: When the edict was ready, Xun would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Xun refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 言官劾其作威植黨。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials impeached him for wielding power and forming factions.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrators impeached him for abusing authority and building a faction.

sentences.zh: 勛疏辯，有「何必更勞賜敕」語。

translations.literal: Xun submitted a memorial in defense containing the words, "Why trouble yourself further to grant an edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun submitted a defense in which he wrote, "Why trouble yourself further to grant an edict?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃大怒，責其「強悖無人臣禮」。

translations.literal: The emperor then grew greatly angry and rebuked him for being "obstinate, perverse, and lacking the rites of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and rebuked him for being "obstinate, defiant, and devoid of a subject's propriety."

sentences.zh: 於是給事中高時盡發勛奸利事，且言交通張延齡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Gao Shi fully exposed Xun's corrupt and profiteering acts and also said he had dealings with Zhang Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gao Shi then laid bare all of Xun's corrupt profiteering and accused him of collusion with Zhang Yanling.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，下勛錦衣獄。

translations.literal: The emperor grew even angrier and sent Xun down to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger deepened, and Xun was thrown into the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月也。

translations.literal: It was the ninth month of the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the ninth month of the twentieth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 尋諭鎮撫司勿加刑訊。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor instructed the prison directorate not to apply torture in interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor ordered the prison directorate not to torture him under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 奏上，當勛死罪。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Xun was judged liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the report was submitted, Xun was found liable to death.

sentences.zh: 帝令法司覆勘。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the judicial offices to review the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the judicial offices to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 而給事中劉大直復勘勛亂政十二罪，請並治。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Dazhi again investigated twelve crimes of Xun's disordering government and requested that all be punished together.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Dazhi added twelve counts of governmental misconduct against Xun and asked that all be prosecuted together.

sentences.zh: 法司乃盡實諸疏中罪狀，當勛罪絞。

translations.literal: The judicial offices then verified all the charges in the memorials and judged Xun liable to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices verified every charge in the memorials and sentenced Xun to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 帝令詳議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 法司更當勛不軌罪斬，沒入妻孥田宅。

translations.literal: The judicial offices again judged Xun liable to decapitation for treasonous conduct and confiscation of his wife, children, fields, and houses.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices then sentenced Xun to decapitation for treason and ordered the confiscation of his family, lands, and property.

sentences.zh: 奏上，留中不下。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was kept at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the report was submitted, the emperor kept it at court and issued no decision.

sentences.zh: 帝意欲寬勛，屢示意指。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was to leniently treat Xun, and he repeatedly gave hints to that effect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to spare Xun and repeatedly signaled his intent.

sentences.zh: 而廷臣惡勛甚，謬為不喻者，更坐勛重辟。

translations.literal: But the court ministers hated Xun deeply; feigning not to understand, they again sentenced Xun to a heavier punishment.
translations.idiomatic: But the court ministers hated Xun bitterly; pretending not to understand the emperor's hints, they imposed an even harsher sentence.

sentences.zh: 明年考察言官，特旨貶高時二級，以風廷臣，廷臣終莫為勛請。

translations.literal: The next year, during the review of remonstrating officials, a special edict demoted Gao Shi two ranks to admonish the court ministers, yet the court ministers in the end never pleaded for Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, during the review of remonstrating officials, a special edict demoted Gao Shi two ranks as a warning to the court, yet no minister ever pleaded for Xun.

sentences.zh: 其冬，勛死獄中。

translations.literal: That winter Xun died in prison.
