translations.idiomatic: That winter Xun died in prison.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，責法司淹系。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and rebuked the judicial offices for prolonged detention.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and rebuked the judicial offices for keeping him imprisoned so long.

sentences.zh: 褫刑部尚書吳山職，侍郎都御史以下鐫降有差，而免勛籍沒，僅奪誥券而已。

translations.literal: He stripped Minister of Justice Wu Shan of his post; vice ministers, censors-in-chief, and those below were demoted by degrees; yet Xun was exempted from confiscation of registers and property, and only his patent of nobility was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Minister of Justice Wu Shan of office; vice ministers, censors-in-chief, and officials below were demoted in varying degrees; yet Xun's property was spared confiscation, and only his patent of nobility was revoked.

sentences.zh: 自明興以來，勛臣不與政事。

translations.literal: Since the rise of the Ming, meritorious ministers did not participate in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, meritorious nobles had not been involved in governance.

sentences.zh: 惟勛以挾恩寵、擅朝權、恣為奸慝致敗。

translations.literal: Only Xun, by relying on favor, monopolizing court power, and willfully committing wickedness, brought ruin upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun alone, by trading on imperial favor, monopolizing court power, and committing wickedness at will, brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 勛死數年，其子守乾嗣侯，傳至曾孫培民。

translations.literal: Several years after Xun's death, his son Shouqian inherited the marquisate, and the line passed down to his great-grandson Peimin.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Xun's death, his son Shouqian inherited the marquisate, and the title passed down to his great-grandson Peimin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，死於賊。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign he was killed by rebels.

sentences.zh: 華雲龍

translations.literal: Hua Yunlong
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yunlong

sentences.zh: 華雲龍，定遠人。

translations.literal: Hua Yunlong was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yunlong came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 聚眾居韭山。

translations.literal: He gathered a band and dwelt on Jiushan.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered followers and made his base on Jiushan.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵，來歸。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor raised his army, he came and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor raised his banner, he came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 從克滁、和，為千夫長。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Chu and He and became commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Chu and He and was made commander of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，破採石水寨及方山營。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, broke the Caishi river stockade and the Fangshan camp.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with the army, stormed the Caishi river stockade, and broke the Fangshan camp.

sentences.zh: 下集慶路，生擒元將，得兵萬人，克鎮江，遷總管。

translations.literal: He took Jiqing Circuit, captured a Yuan general alive, obtained ten thousand troops, captured Zhenjiang, and was transferred to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiqing Circuit, captured a Yuan general alive, seized ten thousand troops, captured Zhenjiang, and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 攻拔廣德，戰舊館，擒湯元帥，進右副元帥。

translations.literal: He attacked and captured Guangde, fought at Jiuguan, captured Marshal Tang, and was promoted to right vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Guangde, fought at Jiuguan, captured Marshal Tang, and was promoted to right vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 龍江之役，雲龍伏石灰山，接戰，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: In the campaign on the Long River, Yunlong lay in ambush at Lime Mountain, joined battle, and casualties were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle on the Long River, Yunlong lay in ambush at Lime Mountain; when battle was joined, casualties were about equal on both sides.

sentences.zh: 雲龍躍馬大呼，搗其中堅，遂大敗友諒兵，乘勝復太平。

translations.literal: Yunlong leapt on his horse and shouted loudly, struck the enemy center, and thereby routed Youliang's troops; pressing the victory, he recovered Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlong spurred his horse forward with a great shout, smashed the enemy center, routed Youliang's army, and pressed on to recover Taiping.

sentences.zh: 從下九江、南昌，分兵攻下瑞州、臨江、吉安。

translations.literal: He followed in the reduction of Jiujiang and Nanchang and sent detachments to attack and take Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Jiujiang and Nanchang, then sent detachments to capture Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，戰彭蠡，平武昌。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Anfeng, fought at Poyang, and pacified Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Anfeng, fought at Poyang, and helped pacify Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 累功至豹韜衛指揮使。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he rose to commander of the Leopard Bow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated merit he rose to commander of the Leopard Bow Guard.

sentences.zh: 從徐達帥兵取高郵，進克淮安，遂命守之，改淮安衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in leading troops to take Gaoyou, advanced to capture Huai'an, was then ordered to garrison it, and was changed to commander of the Huai'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in taking Gaoyou, advanced to capture Huai'an, was ordered to garrison the city, and was appointed commander of the Huai'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋攻嘉興，降吳將宋興。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he attacked Jiaxing and received the surrender of Wu general Song Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he attacked Jiaxing and accepted the surrender of Wu general Song Xing.

sentences.zh: 圍平江，軍於胥門。

translations.literal: He besieged Pingjiang and encamped at Xu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Pingjiang and stationed his army at Xu Gate.

sentences.zh: 從大軍北征，徇下山東郡縣，與徐達會帥通州，進克元都。

translations.literal: He followed the main army on the northern expedition, reduced the commanderies and counties of Shandong, joined Xu Da in commanding at Tongzhou, and advanced to capture the Yuan capital.
translations.idiomatic: He marched north with the main army, subduing the cities and counties of Shandong, joined Xu Da in command at Tongzhou, and advanced to take the Yuan capital.

sentences.zh: 擢大都督府僉事，總六衛兵留守兼北平行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Grand Military Commission, put in overall charge of the garrison troops of six guards while remaining to hold the frontier, and concurrently made assistant administrator of the Beiping Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted vice commissioner of the Grand Military Commission, given command of the six guards' garrison forces left to hold the north, and appointed assistant administrator of the Beiping Branch Secretariat as well.

sentences.zh: 逾年，攻下雲州，獲平章火兒忽答、右丞哈海。

translations.literal: After a year he attacked and took Yunzhou, capturing Pacification Commissioner Huo'erhuda and Vice Administrator Hahai.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he stormed Yunzhou and captured the Yuan pacification commissioner Huo'erhuda and vice administrator Hahai.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知，兼燕王左相。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the chief command and concurrently served as left chancellor to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy chief commander and appointed left chancellor to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年冬，論功封淮安侯，祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Hongwu, his merit was assessed and he was enfeoffed Marquis of Huai'an with a stipend of one thousand five hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent of exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Hongwu's third year, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Huai'an with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and a hereditary patent of exemption, in recognition of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 雲龍上言：「北平邊塞，東自永平、薊州，西至灰嶺下，隘口一百二十一，相去可二千二百里。

translations.literal: Yunlong submitted a memorial: 「The Beiping frontier runs from Yongping and Jizhou in the east to below Huiling in the west, with one hundred twenty-one passes spanning roughly two thousand two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlong submitted a memorial: 「On the Beiping frontier, from Yongping and Jizhou in the east to the foot of Huiling in the west, there are one hundred twenty-one passes over some two thousand two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其王平口至官坐嶺，隘口九，相去五百余里。

translations.literal: From Wangping Pass to Guanzuo Ridge alone, there are nine passes spanning more than five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: From Wangping Pass to Guanzuo Ridge alone there are nine passes over more than five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 俱衝要，宜設兵。

translations.literal: All are strategically vital; troops should be posted there.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of them is vital; troops ought to be stationed there.

sentences.zh: 紫荊關及蘆花山嶺尤要害，宜設千戶守御所。」

translations.literal: Zijing Pass and Luhua Mountain Ridge are especially critical; battalion command garrisons should be established there.」
translations.idiomatic: Zijing Pass and Luhua Mountain Ridge are above all the keys to the line; battalion garrisons should be set up to hold them.」

sentences.zh: 又言：「前大兵克永平，留故元八翼軍士千六百人屯田，人月支糧五斗，所得不償費。

translations.literal: He further said: 「When the army earlier took Yongping, sixteen hundred soldiers of the former Yuan Eight Wings were left to farm garrison lands; each man received five dou of grain per month, yet the yield did not cover the cost.
translations.idiomatic: He added: 「When our army first took Yongping, sixteen hundred men of the old Yuan Eight Wings were kept on garrison farms, each drawing five dou of grain a month — yet the harvest never paid for the expense.

sentences.zh: 宜入燕山諸衛，補伍操練。」

translations.literal: They should be absorbed into the Yan Mountain guards, assigned to fill out the ranks, and drilled.」
translations.idiomatic: They should be absorbed into the Yan Mountain guards, slotted into the ranks, and put through regular drill.」

sentences.zh: 俱從之。

translations.literal: Both proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Both recommendations were approved.

sentences.zh: 行邊至雲州，襲元平章僧家奴營於牙頭，突入其帳擒之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: On a frontier tour he reached Yunzhou, raided the camp of the Yuan pacification commissioner Sengjianu at Yatou, burst into his tent and seized him, and took all his troops captive.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the frontier he reached Yunzhou, struck the camp of the Yuan pacification commissioner Sengjianu at Yatou, burst into his tent to capture him, and took his entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 至上都大石崖，攻克劉學士諸寨，驢兒國公奔漠北。

translations.literal: At the Great Stone Cliff of the Upper Capital he stormed the stockades of Liu the Scholar; the State Duke Lü'er fled into the northern deserts.
translations.idiomatic: At the Great Stone Cliff near the Upper Capital he overran the stockades commanded by Liu the Scholar, and the State Duke Lü'er fled deep into the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 自是無內犯者，威名大著。

translations.literal: From then on there were no further raids into the interior, and his renown was greatly established.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Yuan made no more incursions into the interior, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 建燕邸，增筑北平城，皆其經畫。

translations.literal: The construction of the Yan princely residence and the enlargement of Beiping city were both planned by him.
translations.idiomatic: He planned the building of the Prince of Yan's residence and the expansion of Beiping's walls.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，有言雲龍據元相脫脫第宅，僭用故元宮中物。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongwu, it was reported that Yunlong occupied the mansion of the Yuan chancellor Toqto and presumptuously used objects from the former Yuan palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's seventh year someone reported that Yunlong had taken over Chancellor Toqto's mansion and was presumptuously using furnishings from the old Yuan palace.

sentences.zh: 召還，命何文輝往代。

translations.literal: He was recalled, and He Wenhui was ordered to go and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlong was recalled to court, and He Wenhui was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未至京，道卒。

translations.literal: Before he reached the capital, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the journey before he ever reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 子中襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 李文忠之卒也，中侍疾進藥，坐貶死。

translations.literal: When Li Wenzhong died, Zhong had attended his illness and administered medicine; for this he was demoted and condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wenzhong died, Zhong had tended him in illness and given him medicine; for this he was demoted and executed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年追論中胡黨，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was retroactively charged with membership in Hu Weiyong's faction, and the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Zhong was posthumously tied to Hu Weiyong's faction, and the title was stripped from the family.

sentences.zh: 韓政，睢人。

translations.literal: Han Zheng was a native of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zheng came from Sui county.

sentences.zh: 嘗為義兵元帥，帥眾歸太祖，授江淮行省平章政事。

translations.literal: He had once served as marshal of a righteous army; he led his troops to submit to the Founding Emperor and was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen as marshal of a local militia, then brought his followers over to the Founding Emperor and was made Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李濟據濠州，名為張士誠守，實觀望。

translations.literal: Li Ji held Haozhou, nominally keeping it for Zhang Shicheng but in fact waiting to see which way the wind would blow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji held Haozhou in Zhang Shicheng's name but was really biding his time to see who would prevail.

sentences.zh: 太祖使右相國李善長以書招之，不報。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had the Right Chancellor Li Shanzhang send him a letter of summons, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Right Chancellor Li Shanzhang with a letter summoning him, but Li Ji gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘆曰：「濠，吾家也，濟如此，我有國無家可乎！」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sighed and said: 「Haozhou is my home — yet Ji acts thus! Can I possess a kingdom and not a home?」
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sighed: 「Haozhou is my own birthplace — and Ji treats me like this! Can I rule an empire yet have no home?」

sentences.zh: 乃命政帥指揮顧時以雲梯砲石四面攻濠。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Zheng to lead Commander Gu Shi in attacking Haozhou from all four sides with scaling ladders and catapults.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zheng and Commander Gu Shi to assault Haozhou from every side with siege ladders and stone-throwing engines.

sentences.zh: 濟度不能支，始出降。

translations.literal: Ji saw that he could not hold out and at last came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not endure the siege, Ji at last surrendered.

sentences.zh: 政歸濟於應天。

translations.literal: Zheng escorted Ji back to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng brought Li Ji to Yingtian in custody.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，以時守濠州。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was greatly pleased and put Gu Shi in charge of garrisoning Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was delighted and left Gu Shi to hold Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 政從徐達攻安豐，扼其四門，潛穴城東龍尾壩，入其城二十余丈。

translations.literal: Zheng followed Xu Da in attacking Anfeng, blocked its four gates, and secretly tunneled through the Longwei Dam east of the city, penetrating more than twenty zhang into the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng joined Xu Da in the assault on Anfeng, sealed all four gates, and drove a mine through the Longwei Dam east of the city until it ran more than twenty zhang under the walls.

sentences.zh: 城壞，遂破之。

translations.literal: The wall collapsed, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The walls gave way and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 元將忻都、竹貞、左君弼皆走。

translations.literal: The Yuan generals Xindu, Zhu Zhen, and Zuo Junbi all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan commanders Xindu, Zhu Zhen, and Zuo Junbi all fled.

sentences.zh: 追奔四十余里，擒都。

translations.literal: The pursuers ran them down for more than forty li and captured Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit covered more than forty li and brought back Xindu in chains.

sentences.zh: 俄而貞引兵來援，與戰城南門，再破走之。

translations.literal: Soon Zhu Zhen brought troops to the rescue; they fought at the south gate, and he was defeated and driven off again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhu Zhen marched to relieve the city; Zheng met him at the south gate, defeated him, and drove him off a second time.

sentences.zh: 淮東、西悉平。

translations.literal: All of eastern and western Huai was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All the lands east and west of the Huai were brought to order.

sentences.zh: 已，從大軍平吳。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed the main army in pacifying Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with the main army to bring Wu to heel.

sentences.zh: 又從北伐，降梁城守將盧斌。

translations.literal: He again joined the northern expedition and received the surrender of Liangcheng's garrison commander Lu Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the northern campaign as well and accepted the surrender of Liangcheng's defender Lu Bin.

sentences.zh: 分兵扼黃河，斷山東援軍，遂取益都、濟寧、濟南，皆有功。

translations.literal: He detached troops to hold the Yellow River, cut off Shandong's relief forces, and then took Yidu, Jining, and Jinan — winning merit in each action.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to hold the Yellow River and sever Shandong's reinforcements, then helped take Yidu, Jining, and Jinan, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 克東平，功尤多，改山東行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the capture of Dongping his merit was especially great, and he was reassigned as Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He played a leading part in the fall of Dongping and was made Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以師會大將軍於臨清，檄政守東昌。

translations.literal: With his army he joined the grand general at Linqing; orders were issued for Zheng to garrison Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his troops to join the grand general at Linqing, then was ordered to hold Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 既下大都，命政分兵守廣平。

translations.literal: After the capital fell, Zheng was ordered to detach troops to hold Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dadu had fallen, he was told to detach a force to garrison Guangping.

sentences.zh: 政遂諭降白土諸寨。

translations.literal: Zheng thereupon persuaded the stockades of Baitu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng then talked the Baitu stockades into submission.

sentences.zh: 移守彰德，下蟻尖寨。

translations.literal: He shifted his garrison to Zhangde and took Yijian Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to garrison Zhangde and captured Yijian Stockade.

sentences.zh: 蟻尖者，在林慮西北二十里，為元右丞吳庸、王居義、小鎖兒所據。

translations.literal: Yijian lay twenty li northwest of Linlu and was held by the Yuan vice administrator Wu Yong, Wang Juyi, and Xiao Suo'er.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian stood twenty li northwest of Linlu, held by the Yuan vice administrator Wu Yong, Wang Juyi, and Xiao Suo'er.

sentences.zh: 大將軍之北伐也，遣將士收復諸山寨，降者相繼，蟻尖獨恃險不下。

translations.literal: When the grand general marched north, he sent officers and soldiers to recover the mountain stockades; surrender followed surrender, but Yijian alone trusted its terrain and refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the grand general's northern campaign, detachments recovered stockade after stockade as commanders came over one after another, but Yijian alone relied on its heights and held out.

sentences.zh: 至是兵逼之，庸誘殺居義及小鎖兒以降，得士卒萬余人。

translations.literal: At this point troops pressed in on it; Wu Yong treacherously killed Wang Juyi and Xiao Suo'er to surrender, yielding more than ten thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng's men closed in, Wu Yong murdered Wang Juyi and Xiao Suo'er in a plot to surrender, delivering more than ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 尋調征陝西，還兵守御河北。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to campaign in Shaanxi, then brought his troops back to defend Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned to the Shaanxi campaign, then returned north to guard Hebei.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封東平侯，祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongping with a stipend of one thousand five hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent of exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's third year he was made Marquis of Dongping with fifteen hundred piculs and a hereditary patent of exemption.

sentences.zh: 移鎮山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to hold Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復移河北。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved again to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was shifted back to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 招撫流民，復業甚眾。

translations.literal: He recruited and settled displaced people, and a great many returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He brought refugees in from the wilds, and vast numbers returned to their fields and trades.

sentences.zh: 從左副將軍李文忠搗應昌，至臚朐河。

translations.literal: He followed the left deputy general Li Wenzhong in a strike against Yingchang as far as the Luchu River.
translations.idiomatic: He marched under Left Deputy General Li Wenzhong on the raid against Yingchang, reaching the Luchu River.

sentences.zh: 文忠深入，令政守輜重。

translations.literal: Wenzhong pressed deep into enemy country and ordered Zheng to guard the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong drove deep into enemy territory and left Zheng to guard the supply train.

sentences.zh: 還，命巡河南、陝西。

translations.literal: On his return he was ordered to inspect Henan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was sent to inspect Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 再從信國公湯和練兵於臨清。

translations.literal: He again followed the Duke of Xin, Tang He, in drilling troops at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Duke of Xin, Tang He, in training troops at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月卒，帝親臨其喪。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he died, and the Emperor attended his funeral in person.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the eleventh year, and the Emperor came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 追封鄆國公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 子勛襲。

translations.literal: His son Xun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Xun succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 二十六年坐藍黨誅，爵除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was executed on account of the Lan Yu faction, and the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was put to death in the Lan Yu purge, and the title was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 仇成，含山人。

translations.literal: Chou Cheng was a native of Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Cheng came from Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 初從軍充萬戶，屢遷至秦淮翼副元帥。

translations.literal: At first he entered military service as commander of ten thousand and was repeatedly promoted until he became deputy marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commander of ten thousand and rose through repeated promotions to deputy marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻安慶，敵固守不戰。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor attacked Anqing, the enemy held firm and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the Founding Emperor's assault on Anqing, the defenders shut themselves in and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 廖永忠、張志雄破其水寨，成以陸兵乘之，遂克安慶。

translations.literal: Liao Yongzhong and Zhang Zhixiong broke their river stockade; Cheng pressed in with land troops and thereby took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongzhong and Zhang Zhixiong smashed the river stockade, and Cheng drove his infantry forward to take Anqing.

sentences.zh: 初，元左丞余闕守安慶，陳友諒將趙普勝陷之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Yuan left administrator Yu Que had held Anqing until the Chen Youliang general Zhao Pusheng seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing had been held by the Yuan left administrator Yu Que until Chen Youliang's general Zhao Pusheng overran it.

sentences.zh: 友諒既殺普勝，元帥余某者襲取之。

translations.literal: After Youliang killed Pusheng, a Marshal Yu seized it back.
translations.idiomatic: After Youliang murdered Pusheng, a Marshal Yu retook the city.

sentences.zh: 張定邊復來犯，余帥走死。

translations.literal: Zhang Dingbian came to attack again; Marshal Yu fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dingbian attacked once more, and Marshal Yu fled to his death.

sentences.zh: 至是以成為橫海指揮同知，守其地。

translations.literal: At this time Cheng was made vice commander of the Transverse Sea Command and assigned to hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was now made vice commander of the Transverse Sea Command and charged with holding Anqing.

sentences.zh: 時左君弼據廬州，羅友賢以池州叛，無為知州董曾陷死，四面皆賊境。

translations.literal: At the time Zuo Junbi held Luzhou, Luo Youxian rebelled at Chizhou, Wuwei prefect Dong Zeng was killed in the fall of the city, and on every side lay enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Junbi held Luzhou, Luo Youxian revolted at Chizhou, Prefect Dong Zeng of Wuwei was killed when the city fell, and enemies pressed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 成撫集軍民，守御嚴密，漢兵不敢東下。

translations.literal: Cheng rallied troops and people, kept the defense strict, and the Han armies did not dare march eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rallied soldiers and civilians, tightened the defenses, and the Han forces did not dare push east.

sentences.zh: 從征鄱陽，殲敵涇江口，功最。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition against Poyang and destroyed the enemy at the mouth of the Jing River; his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Poyang campaign and annihilated the enemy at the mouth of the Jing River, winning the highest distinction.

sentences.zh: 征平江，敗張士誠兵於城西南。

translations.literal: On the expedition against Pingjiang he defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Pingjiang he routed Zhang Shicheng's army southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，僉大都督府事，鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was appointed to the Grand Military Commission and put in command of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's third year he joined the Grand Military Commission and was posted to hold Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 久之，以屯戍無功，降永平衛指揮使。

translations.literal: After a long time, because his garrison farming yielded no merit, he was demoted to commander of the Yongping Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In time, judged to have achieved nothing in garrison farming, he was reduced to commander of the Yongping Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋復官。

translations.literal: Before long his rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 十二年論藍玉等征西功，當封。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the western campaign merit of Lan Yu and others was assessed, he should have been enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when honors for Lan Yu's western campaign were under discussion, he was due a title.

sentences.zh: 帝念成舊勛，先封為安慶侯，歲祿二千石。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful of Cheng's old service, first enfeoffed him Marquis of Anqing with an annual stipend of two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Cheng's earlier achievements, the Emperor enfeoffed him first as Marquis of Anqing with two thousand piculs a year.

sentences.zh: 二十年充征南副將軍，討平容美諸峒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he served as deputy southern expeditionary general and suppressed Rongmei and the other mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he served as deputy southern expeditionary general and pacified Rongmei and the other fortified valleys.

sentences.zh: 復從大軍征雲南，功多，予世券，加祿五百石。

translations.literal: He again followed the main army against Yunnan; his merit was great, and he was granted a hereditary patent of exemption and an additional stipend of five hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again on Yunnan with the main army, won great distinction, and received a hereditary patent plus five hundred piculs added to his stipend.

sentences.zh: 二十一年七月，有疾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-first year he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 賜內醞，手詔存問。

translations.literal: He was granted imperial wine, and a personal edict was sent to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted him imperial wine and wrote a personal edict to inquire after his condition.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈皖國公，諡庄襄。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Wan with the posthumous title Zhuangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously created Duke of Wan with the posthumous name Zhuangxiang.

sentences.zh: 子正襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 張龍，濠人。

translations.literal: Zhang Long was a native of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Long came from Hao.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，定常州、寧國、婺州，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river and in securing Changzhou, Ningguo, and Wuzhou, winning merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with the army and helped secure Changzhou, Ningguo, and Wuzhou, distinguishing himself throughout.

sentences.zh: 從征江州，為都先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition against Jiangzhou and served as overall vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiangzhou campaign he served as chief vanguard.

sentences.zh: 平武昌，授花槍所千戶。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was pacified he was appointed commander of a thousand in the Flower Spear unit.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell he was made commander of a thousand in the Flower Spear corps.

sentences.zh: 從平淮東，守御海安。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying eastern Huai and was assigned to garrison Hai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Huai east and was posted to defend Hai'an.

sentences.zh: 與張士誠將戰於海口，擒彭元帥，俘其卒數百。

translations.literal: He fought Zhang Shicheng's general at Haikou, captured Marshal Peng, and took several hundred of his soldiers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: At Haikou he fought one of Zhang Shicheng's generals, captured Marshal Peng, and took several hundred of his men prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進攻通州，擊斬賊將。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Tongzhou, struck down and killed a rebel general.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Tongzhou and killed a rebel general in battle.

sentences.zh: 擢威武衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Weiwu Guard command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted vice commander of the Weiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 從平山東、河南。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He helped bring Shandong and Henan to order.

sentences.zh: 大兵克潼關，以龍為副留守。

translations.literal: When the army took Tong Pass, Long was made deputy garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong Pass fell, Long was appointed deputy garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年調守鳳翔，改鳳翔衛指揮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang and was changed to commander of the Fengxiang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's third year he was posted to Fengxiang and made commander of the Fengxiang Guard.

sentences.zh: 賀宗哲悉眾圍城，龍固守。

translations.literal: He Zongzhe brought his entire force to besiege the city, and Long held firm.
translations.idiomatic: He Zongzhe marched up with his full strength to siege the city, and Long held fast inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 宗哲攻北門，龍出兵搏戰，矢傷右脅，不為動。

translations.literal: Zongzhe attacked the north gate; Long sallied forth to grapple in battle, was wounded by an arrow in the right flank, and did not stir from his place.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhe assaulted the north gate; Long led a sortie and fought hand to hand, took an arrow in the right flank, and never flinched.

sentences.zh: 遂大敗之。

translations.literal: He thereupon inflicted a great defeat on the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He then routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 進克鳳州，擒李參政等二十余人。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Fengzhou and captured Vice Administrator Li and more than twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to capture Fengzhou, seizing Vice Administrator Li and more than twenty others.

sentences.zh: 大將軍達入沔州，遣龍別將一軍，由鳳翔入連雲棧，攻興元，降其守將劉思忠。

translations.literal: Grand General Da entered Mianzhou, dispatched Long as a separate commander with one army, entered by way of Fengxiang through the Lianyun plank road, attacked Xingyuan, and induced its defending general Liu Sizhong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Xu Da entered Mianzhou, he sent Long with a detached force through Fengxiang along the Lianyun plank road to attack Xingyuan, where the defending general Liu Sizhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蜀將吳友仁來犯，龍擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shu general Wu Youren came to attack; Long struck and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu general Wu Youren marched against him, Long repulsed the attack.

sentences.zh: 友仁復悉兵薄城，大治攻具。

translations.literal: Youren again brought his entire force to press close to the city and greatly prepared siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Youren returned with his full strength, pressed up to the walls, and set about preparing a major assault.

sentences.zh: 龍從北門突出，繞友仁軍後，敵盡棄甲仗走，自是不復窺興元。

translations.literal: Long burst out from the north gate, circled behind Youren's army, the enemy all cast off armor and weapons and fled, and from then on did not again cast eyes on Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Long sallied from the north gate, swung behind Youren's army, and routed the enemy so completely that they threw down arms and fled; after that they never threatened Xingyuan again.

sentences.zh: 召僉大都督府事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve in the Grand Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to join the Grand Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 十一年副李文忠征西番洮州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as deputy to Li Wenzhong in campaigning against the western tribes at Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served under Li Wenzhong in the campaign against the western tribes at Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 論功，封鳳翔侯，祿二千石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengxiang with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary commandership.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengxiang with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary rank as commander.

sentences.zh: 復從傅友德征雲南，鎮七星關，破大理、鶴慶，平諸洞蠻。

translations.literal: He again followed Fu Youde against Yunnan, garrisoned Qixing Pass, broke Dali and Heqing, and pacified the various cave tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again with Fu Youde into Yunnan, held Qixing Pass, captured Dali and Heqing, and pacified the cave tribes of the region.

sentences.zh: 加祿五百石，予世券三十年。

translations.literal: Five hundred piculs were added to his stipend, and he was granted a hereditary patent of exemption valid for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: His stipend was increased by five hundred piculs, and he received a hereditary patent of exemption good for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 二十年從馮勝出金山，降納哈出。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed Feng Sheng out from Jinshan and accepted the surrender of Nahachu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he followed Feng Sheng on the Jinshan expedition and helped accept Nahachu's surrender.

sentences.zh: 明年，勝調降軍征雲南，次常德，叛去。

translations.literal: The next year Feng Sheng mobilized the surrendered troops for the Yunnan campaign; when they halted at Changde they rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Feng Sheng led the surrendered troops south toward Yunnan, but at Changde they mutinied and broke away.

sentences.zh: 龍追至重慶，收捕之。

translations.literal: Long pursued them to Chongqing and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Long pursued them to Chongqing and rounded them up.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春同延安侯唐勝宗督屯田於平越、鎮遠、貴州，議置龍里衛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year, together with Tang Sheng Zong, Marquis of Yan'an, he supervised military colonies at Pingyue, Zhenyuan, and Guizhou, and it was proposed to establish the Longli Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year he joined Yan'an Marquis Tang Sheng Zong in supervising military colonies at Pingyue, Zhenyuan, and Guizhou, where the establishment of the Longli Guard was proposed.

sentences.zh: 都勻亂，佐藍玉討平之。

translations.literal: When Duyun rose in revolt, he assisted Lan Yu in suppressing and pacifying it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duyun rebelled, he assisted Lan Yu in putting down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 以老疾請告。

translations.literal: Because of age and illness he requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: Growing old and ill, he asked to retire from duty.

sentences.zh: 三十年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: 子麟尚福清公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Lin married Princess Fuqing and was appointed Commandant of the Consort's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin married Princess Fuqing and was made Commandant of the Consort's Guard.

sentences.zh: 孫傑侍公主京師。

translations.literal: His grandson Jie attended the princess in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Jie waited upon the princess in the capital.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，失侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign the marquisate was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign the family lost the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 傑子嗣，宣德十年，援詔恩乞嗣。

translations.literal: Jie's son Si, in the tenth year of Xuande, appealed to an edict of grace to beg succession to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's son Si, in Xuande's tenth year, invoked an edict of grace to petition for restoration of the title.

sentences.zh: 吏部言：龍侯不嗣者四十年，不許。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel reported: the Marquis of Long line has gone without succession for forty years—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel replied that the Marquis of Long title had lapsed for forty years and could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 吳復，字伯起，合肥人。

translations.literal: Wu Fu, styled Boqi, was a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fu, whose style was Boqi, came from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 少負勇略。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he showed both courage and tactical skill.

sentences.zh: 元末，集眾保鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he gathered followers to protect his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he raised a band to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖於濠，從克泗、滁、和、採石、太平，累官萬戶。

translations.literal: He submitted to the Founding Emperor at Hao and followed in capturing Si, Chu, He, Caishi, and Taiping, rising through successive posts to commander of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Founding Emperor at Hao and followed the conquest of Si, Chu, He, Caishi, and Taiping, rising through repeated promotions to commander of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 從破蠻子海牙水寨，定集慶。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Manzi Haiya's river stockade and securing Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped break Manzi Haiya's river stockade and secure Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 從徐達攻鎮江，斬元平章定定。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in attacking Zhenjiang and beheaded the Yuan Minister of the Interior Ding Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xu Da he attacked Zhenjiang and beheaded the Yuan minister Ding Ding.

sentences.zh: 下丹陽、金壇，克常州，進統軍元帥。

translations.literal: He reduced Danyang and Jintan, took Changzhou, and was promoted to army commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He took Danyang and Jintan, captured Changzhou, and was promoted army commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 徇江陰、無錫，還守常州。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Jiangyin and Wuxi, then returned to garrison Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned through Jiangyin and Wuxi, then returned to hold Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 張士誠兵奄至，力戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng's troops suddenly arrived; he fought fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng's army suddenly appeared, he fought hard and drove it off.

sentences.zh: 追奔至長興，連敗之於高橋、太湖及忠節門，士誠奪氣。

translations.literal: He pursued the fleeing enemy to Changxing and repeatedly defeated them at Gaoqiao, Taihu, and Zhongjie Gate, and Shicheng lost his fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fugitives to Changxing and defeated them again at Gaoqiao, Taihu, and Zhongjie Gate, until Shicheng lost heart.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，平武昌。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Anfeng and the pacification of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Anfeng and the pacification of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 從徐達克廬州，下漢、沔、荊諸郡縣。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Luzhou and reducing the various prefectures and counties of Han, Mian, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xu Da he captured Luzhou and then reduced the Han, Mian, and Jing prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 授鎮武衛指揮同知，守沔陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commander of the Zhenwu Guard and posted to defend Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commander of the Zhenwu Guard and posted to defend Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春下襄陽，別將破安陸，擒元同僉任亮，遂守之。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in taking Xiangyang; as a separate commander he broke Anlu, captured the Yuan assistant commissioner Ren Liang, and then garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chang Yuchun in the capture of Xiangyang, then as a detached commander broke Anlu, seized the Yuan assistant commissioner Ren Liang, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 克汝州、魯山。

translations.literal: He took Ruzhou and Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ruzhou and Lushan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從傅友德征雲南，克普定，城水西。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed Fu Youde against Yunnan, took Puding, and walled Shuixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he marched with Fu Youde into Yunnan, captured Puding, and fortified Shuixi.

sentences.zh: 充總兵官，剿捕諸蠻。

translations.literal: He served as overall army commander and hunted down the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall commander and led campaigns to suppress the tribal forces.

sentences.zh: 遂由關索嶺開箐道，取廣西。

translations.literal: He then opened a path through the ravines by way of Guansuo Ridge and seized Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut a route through the ravines at Guansuo Ridge and advanced into Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十六年克墨定苗，至吉剌堡，築安庄、新城，平七百房諸寨，斬獲萬計，轉餉盤江。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he subdued the Moding Miao, reached Jila Fort, built Anzhuang and Xincheng, pacified the seven hundred-odd stockades, killed and captured to the number of ten thousand, and transported grain to Panjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he subdued the Moding Miao, reached Jila Fort, built Anzhuang and Xincheng, pacified more than seven hundred stockades with kills and captures numbering in the tens of thousands, and moved supplies to the Pan River.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，金瘡發，卒於普定。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year an old wound reopened and he died at Puding.
translations.idiomatic: That October an old battle wound reopened, and he died at Puding.

sentences.zh: 追封黔國公，諡威毅，加祿五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qian, with the posthumous title Weiyi, five hundred piculs were added to his stipend, and he was granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Duke of Qian with the posthumous name Weiyi, given five hundred piculs added to his stipend, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 復臨陣奮發，沖犯矢石，體無完膚。

translations.literal: Fu in battle was always roused to ardor, rushing against arrows and stones until no part of his body remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Fu always fought with fierce ardor, charging through arrows and stones until his body was covered with wounds.

sentences.zh: 平居恂恂，口不言征伐事。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was deferential and restrained, and did not speak of campaigns and battles.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was modest and quiet, and never spoke of war.

sentences.zh: 在普定買妾楊氏，年十七。

translations.literal: At Puding he purchased a concubine surnamed Yang, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: At Puding he bought a concubine named Yang, seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 復死，視殮畢，沐浴更衣，自經死。

translations.literal: When Fu died, after viewing the encoffining to its completion she bathed, changed clothes, and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, she watched the encoffining through to the end, then bathed, changed her clothes, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 封貞烈淑人。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Lady Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted the title Lady Zhenlie, Chaste and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 附 周武

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhou Wu
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhou Wu

sentences.zh: 初，與復以征西番功侯者，又有周武。

translations.literal: At the beginning, among those enfeoffed as marquises for merit in campaigning against the western tribes along with Fu, there was also Zhou Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Among those enfeoffed as marquises for the western campaign along with Fu, there was also Zhou Wu.

sentences.zh: 武，開州人，從定江東，滅漢，收淮東，平吳，積功為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Wu was a native of Kaizhou; he followed in settling Jiangdong, destroying Han, recovering eastern Huai, and pacifying Wu, and through accumulated merit became vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wu came from Kaizhou. He helped secure Jiangdong, destroy the Han regime, recover eastern Huai, and pacify Wu, rising through accumulated merit to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從定中原，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed in settling the Central Plain and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the conquest of the Central Plain and was promoted vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年以參將從沐英討西番朵甘，功多。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu, as deputy general he followed Mu Ying against the western tribes of Duogan and won great merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu's eleventh year he served as deputy general under Mu Ying against the western tribes of Duogan and won great distinction.

sentences.zh: 師還，封雄武侯，祿二千石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiongwu with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary commandership.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made Marquis of Xiongwu with a stipend of two thousand piculs and hereditary rank as commander.

sentences.zh: 出理河南軍務，巡撫北邊。

translations.literal: He went out to administer Henan military affairs and toured the northern frontier as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to handle Henan military affairs and to inspect the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十三年卒，贈汝國公，諡勇襄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died; posthumously he was made Duke of Ru with the posthumous title Yongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year and was posthumously made Duke of Ru with the posthumous name Yongxiang.

sentences.zh: 胡海，字海洋，定遠人。

translations.literal: Hu Hai, styled Haiyang, was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hai, whose style was Haiyang, came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗入土豪赤塘王總管營，自拔來歸，授百戶。

translations.literal: Once he entered the camp of the local strongman Prefect Wang of Chitang, broke free and came over in surrender, and was appointed centurion.
translations.idiomatic: He once entered the camp of the local strongman Prefect Wang of Chitang, broke away on his own, came over to the Ming side, and was made a centurion.

sentences.zh: 從敗元將賈魯兵，克泗、滁，進萬戶。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating the troops of the Yuan general Jia Lu, took Si and Chu, and was promoted to commander of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat the Yuan general Jia Lu, captured Si and Chu, and was promoted commander of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，拔蠻子海牙水寨，破陳埜先兵，從取集慶、鎮江。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, seized Manzi Haiya's river stockade, broke Chen Yexian's army, and followed in taking Jiqing and Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with the army, seized Manzi Haiya's river stockade, routed Chen Yexian's forces, and helped take Jiqing and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 敗元將謝國璽於寧國，選充先鋒。

translations.literal: He defeated the Yuan general Xie Guoxi at Ningguo and was selected to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At Ningguo he defeated the Yuan general Xie Guoxi and was chosen for the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從大軍圍湖州，墮其東南門月城。

translations.literal: He followed the main army in besieging Huzhou and stormed the outer rampart at the southeast gate.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Huzhou and stormed the crescent rampart at the southeast gate.

sentences.zh: 從攻宜興，下婺州，鏖戰紹興，生得賊四百余人，進都先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Yixing, took Wuzhou, fought hard at Shaoxing, took more than four hundred rebels alive, and was promoted to chief vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Yixing, captured Wuzhou, battled fiercely at Shaoxing, took more than four hundred enemy soldiers alive, and was promoted chief vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又從戰龍江，克安慶，與漢人相持，八戰，皆大捷，遂入江州。

translations.literal: He again fought at Longjiang, took Anqing, and locked in stalemate with the Han forces; in eight battles he won great victories each time, and then entered Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Longjiang, captured Anqing, and grappled with the Han armies in eight successive major victories before entering Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 從徐達攻廬州，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in attacking Luzhou and won merit in every action.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xu Da he besieged Luzhou and distinguished himself throughout.

sentences.zh: 海驍勇，屢戰屢傷，手足胸腹間金痍皆遍，而斗益力。

translations.literal: Hai was fierce and brave; battle after battle he was wounded until old battle scars covered his hands, feet, chest, and belly, yet he fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Hai was ferociously brave. Wounded again and again, his hands, feet, chest, and belly were mapped with old battle scars, yet he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 士卒從之者無不激勵自效。

translations.literal: Soldiers who followed him were all stirred to give their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier who served under him was roused to fight with all he had.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之，授花槍上千戶。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor admired his prowess and appointed him commander of a thousand in the Flower Spear corps.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was impressed by his valor and made him commander of a thousand in the Flower Spear corps.

sentences.zh: 復從大軍克荊、澧、衡、潭，擢寶慶衛指揮僉事，遷指揮使，命鎮益陽。

translations.literal: He again followed the main army in taking Jing, Li, Heng, and Tan, was promoted to vice commander of the Baqing Guard, transferred to commander, and ordered to garrison Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again with the main army to capture Jing, Li, Heng, and Tan, was promoted vice commander of the Baqing Guard and then full commander, and was posted to garrison Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 從平章楊璟征湖南、廣西未下郡縣。

translations.literal: He followed Minister Yang Jing in campaigning against the unreduced prefectures and counties of Hunan and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister Yang Jing in reducing the remaining prefectures and counties of Hunan and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 由祁陽進圍永州，與守兵戰於東鄉橋，生得千、萬戶四人，以夜半先登拔之。

translations.literal: Advancing from Qiyang he besieged Yongzhou; fighting the garrison at Dongxiang Bridge he took four commanders of thousands and ten thousands alive, and at midnight led the first assault over the walls and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing from Qiyang he besieged Yongzhou, fought the garrison at Dongxiang Bridge, captured four enemy commanders alive, and at midnight led the first assault over the walls to take the city.

sentences.zh: 抵靖江，戰南門，生得萬戶二人。

translations.literal: Reaching Jingjiang he fought at the south gate and took two commanders of ten thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingjiang he fought at the south gate and captured two commanders of ten thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓，自北門八角亭先登，功最，命為左副總兵。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night he led the first assault over the walls from the Bajiao Pavilion at the north gate; his merit was foremost, and he was appointed left deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch he led the first assault over the walls from the Bajiao Pavilion at the north gate. His merit ranked first, and he was made left deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 剿平左江上思蠻。

translations.literal: He hunted down and pacified the Shangsi tribes of the Zuo River.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the Shangsi tribes along the Zuo River.

sentences.zh: 調征蜀，克龍伏隘、天門山及溫湯關，予世襲指揮使，仍鎮益陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred for the Shu campaign, took Longfu Pass, Tianmen Mountain, and Wentang Pass, was granted hereditary commandership, and still garrisoned Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Shu campaign, he captured Longfu Pass, Tianmen Mountain, and Wentang Pass, was granted hereditary commandership, and continued to garrison Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 武岡、靖州、五開諸苗蠻先後作亂，悉捕誅首亂而撫其餘眾，遷都督僉事。

translations.literal: The Miao tribes of Wugang, Jingzhou, Wukai, and elsewhere successively rebelled; he captured and executed the ringleaders while pacifying the rest, and was transferred to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao of Wugang, Jingzhou, Wukai, and neighboring districts rose in succession, he executed the ringleaders and pacified the rest, and was promoted vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年從征雲南，由永寧趨烏撒，進克可渡河。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the campaign against Yunnan, pressing from Yongning toward Wusa and advancing to take Kehedu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined the Yunnan campaign, pressing from Yongning toward Wusa and capturing the Kehedu crossing.

sentences.zh: 與副將軍沐英會師攻大理，敵悉眾扼上、下關。

translations.literal: He joined Deputy General Mu Ying to attack Dali; the enemy massed their full strength to hold the Upper and Lower Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Deputy General Mu Ying in the assault on Dali, where the enemy concentrated their full strength to hold the upper and lower passes.

sentences.zh: 定遠侯王弼自洱水東趨上關，英帥大軍趨下關，而遣海以夜四鼓取石門。

translations.literal: Dingyuan Marquis Wang Bi pressed toward Upper Pass from east of Erhai Lake; Ying led the main army toward Lower Pass while dispatching Hai at the fourth watch of the night to take Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan Marquis Wang Bi advanced on Upper Pass from east of Erhai Lake, while Mu Ying led the main force against Lower Pass and sent Hai at the fourth watch to seize Shimen.

sentences.zh: 間道渡河，繞點蒼山後，攀大樹緣崖而上，立旂幟。

translations.literal: By a hidden route he crossed the river, circled behind Cangshan, climbed great trees and scaled the cliffs, and raised banners.
translations.idiomatic: By a hidden route he crossed the river, circled behind Cangshan, climbed trees and scaled the cliffs, and raised his banners.

sentences.zh: 英士卒望見，皆踴躍大呼，敵眾驚擾。

translations.literal: Ying's soldiers saw them and all leaped up with loud shouts; the enemy masses were thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ying's troops saw the banners and erupted in cheers; the enemy ranks fell into panic.

sentences.zh: 英遂斬關入。

translations.literal: Ying thereupon broke through the pass and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ying then broke through the pass and entered the city.

sentences.zh: 海亦麾山上軍馳下，前後夾攻，敵悉潰走。

translations.literal: Hai also directed the troops on the mountain to charge down; attacked from front and rear, the enemy all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hai then sent the troops on the heights charging down the slope; caught between two forces, the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 十七年，論功封東川侯，祿二千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchuan with a stipend of twenty-five hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, for his service, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongchuan with a stipend of twenty-five hundred piculs and a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，以左參將從征金山。

translations.literal: More than three years later, as left deputy general he followed the campaign at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he served as left deputy general on the Jinshan campaign.

sentences.zh: 又二年，以征南將軍討平澧州九溪諸蠻寇。

translations.literal: Two years after that, as General Who Conquers the South he suppressed and pacified the various tribal raiders of Lizhou and Jiuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after that, as General Who Conquers the South, he put down the tribal raiders of Lizhou and the Nine Streams.

sentences.zh: 師還，乞歸鄉里，厚賚金帛以行。

translations.literal: When the army returned he begged to go home to his native place and was richly rewarded with gold and silk for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he asked to retire to his home district and was sent off with a rich gift of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 二十四年七月，病疽卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year he died of carbuncle disease, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died of a festering wound in the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 長子斌，龍虎衛指揮使，從征雲南。

translations.literal: His eldest son Bin was commander of the Longhu Guard and followed the campaign against Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bin, commander of the Longhu Guard, joined the Yunnan campaign.

sentences.zh: 過曲靖，猝遇寇，中飛矢卒。

translations.literal: Passing through Qujing he suddenly encountered bandits, was struck by a flying arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Near Qujing he suddenly ran into raiders, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈都督同知。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made assistant commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted assistant commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 次玉，坐藍黨死。

translations.literal: The second son Yu was put to death on account of the Lan Yu faction.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yu was executed in the Lan Yu purge.

sentences.zh: 次觀，尚南康公主，為駙馬都尉，未嗣卒。

translations.literal: The third son Guan married Princess Nankang and served as Commandant of the Consort's Guard; he died without leaving an heir.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Guan married Princess Nankang and served as Commandant of the Consort's Guard, but died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，公主乞以子忠嗣。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign the princess begged that her son Zhong might succeed to the title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign the princess petitioned that her son Zhong be allowed to succeed to the line.

sentences.zh: 詔授孝陵衛指揮僉事，予世襲。

translations.literal: By edict he was appointed vice commander of the Xiaoling Guard and granted hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial edict he was appointed vice commander of the Xiaoling Guard with hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 張赫，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Zhang He was a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He came from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 江淮大亂，團義兵以捍鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Jiang-Huai region fell into great chaos, he organized a volunteer militia to defend his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiang-Huai region plunged into chaos, he raised a volunteer militia to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 嘉山繆把頭招之，不往。

translations.literal: Miao Batou of Jiashan invited him, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Batou of Jiashan tried to recruit him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 聞太祖起，帥眾來附。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Founding Emperor had risen, he led his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the Founding Emperor had raised his banner, he led his followers to join him.

sentences.zh: 授千戶，以功進萬戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of a thousand and, for merit, was promoted to commander of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of a thousand and, for his service, promoted commander of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，所至攻伐皆預，以功擢常春翼元帥，守御常州。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, took part in every assault wherever the army went, and for merit was promoted to Marshal of the Evergreen Wing and assigned to garrison and defend Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangtze with the army, fought in every assault along the way, and for his merit was promoted Marshal of the Evergreen Wing and posted to defend Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋從戰鄱陽，攻武昌。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed in the battle at Poyang and attacked Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fought at Poyang and took part in the assault on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 已，又從大將軍伐張士誠，進圍平江。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again followed the Grand General in attacking Zhang Shicheng and advanced to besiege Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the Grand General's campaign against Zhang Shicheng and helped press the siege of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 諸將分門而軍，赫軍閶門。

translations.literal: The generals divided their forces by gate to encamp; He's army held Chang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The generals assigned each gate to a separate encampment; He took Chang Gate.

sentences.zh: 士誠屢出兵突戰，屢挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Shicheng repeatedly sent troops out in sudden attacks; He repeatedly blunted their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng launched repeated sallies; each time He drove them back.

sentences.zh: 又從大軍克慶元，並下溫、台。

translations.literal: He again followed the main army in capturing Qingyuan and also took Wenzhou and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the main force in taking Qingyuan and helped bring Wenzhou and Taizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，擢福州衛都指揮副使，進本衛同知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was promoted to vice commander of the Fuzhou Guard and advanced to assistant commander of that guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu he was made vice commander of the Fuzhou Guard and then assistant commander of the same command.

sentences.zh: 覆命署都指揮使司事。

translations.literal: Upon returning to audience he was ordered to handle the affairs of the regional military commission in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: On reporting back, he was assigned to administer the regional military commission in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 是時，倭寇出沒海島中，乘間輒傅岸剽掠，沿海居民患苦之。

translations.literal: At that time Japanese pirates appeared and vanished among the sea islands; seizing opportunities they would come ashore to raid and plunder, and the coastal people suffered bitterly from them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Japanese raiders haunted the offshore islands, slipping ashore whenever they found an opening to pillage the coast, to the great misery of local people.

sentences.zh: 帝數遣使齎詔書諭日本國王，又數絕日本貢使，然竟不得倭人要領。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly sent envoys bearing edicts to instruct the king of Japan, and repeatedly cut off Japanese tribute missions, yet in the end could not grasp the pirates' essential nature.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly sent envoys with edicts to the Japanese king and repeatedly barred Japanese tribute missions, yet still could not get to the root of the piracy problem.

sentences.zh: 赫在海上久，所捕倭不可勝計。

translations.literal: He had long been at sea; the pirates he captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He spent long years on the water and captured more pirates than could be counted.

sentences.zh: 最後追寇至琉球大洋，與戰，擒其魁十八人，斬首數十級，獲倭船十余艘，收弓刀器械無算。

translations.literal: At last he pursued the raiders to the open sea off Ryukyu, fought them, captured eighteen of their chiefs, took several tens of heads, seized more than ten pirate ships, and recovered countless bows, blades, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In a final pursuit he chased the raiders to the open seas off Ryukyu, defeated them in battle, took eighteen of their leaders prisoner, severed several dozen heads, captured more than ten enemy ships, and seized an incalculable haul of bows, blades, and arms.

sentences.zh: 帝偉赫功，命掌都指揮印。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired He's achievement and ordered him to hold the seal of the regional military commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised He's exploits and put him in charge of the regional commander's seal.

sentences.zh: 尋調興化衛。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Xinghua Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Xinghua Guard.

sentences.zh: 召還，擢大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he was promoted to vice director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted vice director of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 會遼東漕運艱，軍食後期，帝深以為慮。

translations.literal: It happened that transport of grain by the Liaodong canal route was difficult, army provisions arrived late, and the Emperor was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time grain shipments to Liaodong by the canal route had become difficult and military rations were arriving late, greatly worrying the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 以赫習海道，命督海運事。

translations.literal: Because He was skilled in sea routes, he was ordered to supervise maritime transport.
translations.idiomatic: Since He knew the sea lanes well, the Emperor appointed him to oversee maritime transport.

sentences.zh: 久之，封航海侯，予世券。

translations.literal: After a long time he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Navigation and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was enfeoffed Marquis of Navigation and given a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 前後往來遼東十二年，凡督十運，勞勩備至，軍中賴以無乏。

translations.literal: Over twelve years he traveled back and forth to Liaodong, supervising ten transport runs in all; his labor and merit were complete in every respect, and the army relied on him so that supplies never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Over twelve years he made the Liaodong run again and again, supervising ten full transport cycles; his exertions were beyond praise, and the army depended on him to keep provisions from running out.

sentences.zh: 病卒，追封恩國公，諡庄簡。

translations.literal: He died of illness; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Enguo with the posthumous title Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Enguo with the posthumous title Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 子榮，從征雲南有功，為水軍右衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Rong followed the campaign against Yunnan with merit and served as commander of the Right Guard of the Naval Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong distinguished himself on the Yunnan campaign and became commander of the Right Guard of the Naval Army.

sentences.zh: 孫釒盬，福建都指揮使。

translations.literal: His grandson served as commander of the Fujian Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson served as commander of the Fujian Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，留鎮交阯。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign he remained to garrison Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he was posted to garrison Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 華高，和州人。

translations.literal: Hua Gao was a native of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Gao came from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 與俞通海等以巢湖水師來附。

translations.literal: Together with Yu Tonghai and others he came with the Chaohu Lake navy to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the Chaohu Lake fleet to join the cause, together with Yu Tonghai and others.

sentences.zh: 從克太平，授總管。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Taiping and was appointed chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Taiping and was made chief steward.

sentences.zh: 從破採石、方山兵。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating the forces at Caishi and Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the victories at Caishi and Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 下集慶、鎮江，遷秦淮翼元帥。

translations.literal: He took Jiqing and Zhenjiang and was transferred to marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiqing and Zhenjiang fell, he was promoted marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.

sentences.zh: 與鄧愈徇廣德。

translations.literal: Together with Deng Yu he pacified Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Deng Yu in pacifying Guangde.

sentences.zh: 守將嚴兵城下，高以數騎挑戰，元兵堅壁不動。

translations.literal: The defending commander drew up strict ranks below the wall; Gao with several horsemen provoked battle, but the Yuan troops held their walls and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander massed troops beneath the walls; Gao rode out with a handful of horsemen to challenge them, but the Yuan forces stayed behind their fortifications and refused to engage.

sentences.zh: 高衝擊大破之，遂取其城，得兵萬人，糧數千斛。

translations.literal: Gao charged and broke them completely, then took their city, obtaining ten thousand troops and several thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Gao then charged, routed them completely, and took the city, gaining ten thousand soldiers and several thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 從平常州，進僉行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Changzhou and was promoted vice director of the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Changzhou and was promoted vice director of the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 副俞通海擊破趙普勝柵江營。

translations.literal: Assisting Yu Tonghai he broke Zhao Pusheng's encampment at Zhanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Yu Tonghai, he helped smash Zhao Pusheng's Zhanjiang camp.

sentences.zh: 再敗陳友諒。

translations.literal: He again defeated Chen Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Chen Youliang again.

sentences.zh: 援長興，克武昌。

translations.literal: He reinforced Changxing and captured Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Changxing and helped capture Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 授湖廣行省左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed left vice administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帥舟師從克淮東，收浙西。

translations.literal: Leading the fleet he followed in capturing Huaidong and recovering western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the fleet he joined the conquest of Huaidong and the recovery of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 進行省平章政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand councillor of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted grand councillor of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封廣德侯，歲祿六百石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde with an annual stipend of six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guangde with a stipend of six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 高性怯，且無子，請得宿衛。

translations.literal: Gao was timid by nature and moreover had no son; he requested to serve in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was timid by nature and childless; he asked to serve in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 有所征討，輒稱疾不行。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a campaign he would claim illness and not go.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a campaign was ordered, he pleaded illness and stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 令練水師，復以不習辭。

translations.literal: Ordered to drill the navy, he again excused himself on grounds of inexperience.
translations.idiomatic: When told to train the navy, he again begged off, claiming lack of experience.

sentences.zh: 帝以故舊優容之。

translations.literal: The Emperor on account of old friendship treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for their old ties, the Emperor indulged him.

sentences.zh: 時諸勛臣多出行邊，惟高不遣。

translations.literal: At that time many meritorious officials were sent out to the frontier, but Gao alone was not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most of the founding peers were sent to serve on the frontier, but Gao was never sent.

sentences.zh: 最後繕廣東邊海城堡，高請行。

translations.literal: At last, when the coastal fortresses of Guangdong were being repaired, Gao requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, when coastal fortifications in Guangdong were to be rebuilt, Gao volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿復自力，甚善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You have roused yourself again — very good.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You have taken initiative again — excellent.

sentences.zh: 四年四月事竣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished in the fourth month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 至瓊州卒。

translations.literal: Reaching Qiongzhou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died upon reaching Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，有言高殖利者，故歲祿獨薄。

translations.literal: At the beginning there had been reports that Gao amassed profit, and therefore his annual stipend alone was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been accusations that Gao profited from trade, which was why his stipend alone was set lower.

sentences.zh: 至是貧不能葬。

translations.literal: By this time he was so poor he could not afford burial.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was too poor to afford a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，命補支祿三百石。

translations.literal: The Emperor took pity on him and ordered a supplementary allotment of three hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on him and ordered an additional stipend of three hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 以無子，納誥券墓中。

translations.literal: Because he had no son, his patent of nobility was placed in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Having no heir, his patent of nobility was buried with him in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 贈巢國公，諡武庄。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Duke of Chaoguo with the posthumous title Wuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Chaoguo with the posthumous title Wuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 授從子岳指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His nephew Yue was appointed vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yue was appointed vice commander.

sentences.zh: 張銓，定遠人。

translations.literal: Zhang Quan was a native of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan came from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 從取太平，定集慶、鎮江、常州、婺州。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Taiping and securing Jiqing, Zhenjiang, Changzhou, and Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Taiping and secure Jiqing, Zhenjiang, Changzhou, and Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 搗江州，戰鄱陽湖，取鄂渚。

translations.literal: He raided Jiangzhou, fought at Poyang Lake, and took Ezhu.
translations.idiomatic: He struck at Jiangzhou, fought on Poyang Lake, and captured Ezhu.

sentences.zh: 收淮東，平吳。

translations.literal: He recovered Huaidong and pacified Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped recover Huaidong and finish the conquest of Wu.

sentences.zh: 累功為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he rose to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was made vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從取中原、燕、晉、秦、蜀，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed in taking the Central Plain, Yan, Jin, Qin, and Shu, and was promoted vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaigns across the Central Plain, Yan, Jin, Qin, and Shu, and was promoted vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 使建齊王府，事竣，副江夏侯周德興征五溪蠻。

translations.literal: He was sent to build the Prince of Qi's palace; when the work was finished he served as deputy to Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing in suppressing the Five Streams tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to build the palace of the Prince of Qi, and when that was done served as deputy to Marquis of Jiangxia Zhou Dexing on the campaign against the Five Streams tribes.

sentences.zh: 已而水盡源、通塔平、散毛諸洞酋作亂，復副德興討平之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the chieftains of the caves of Shuijinyuan, Tongtapu, and Sanmao rebelled, and he again served as Dexing's deputy to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the chieftains of Shuijinyuan, Tongtapu, Sanmao, and other mountain strongholds rose in revolt, he again served under Dexing and put them down.

sentences.zh: 從征雲南，由永寧克烏撒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Yunnan and through Yongning captured Wusa.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yunnan campaign he advanced through Yongning and took Wusa.

sentences.zh: 久之，復從傅友德平烏撒及曲靖、普定、龍海、孟定諸蠻。

translations.literal: After a long time he again followed Fu Youde in pacifying Wusa and the various tribes of Qujing, Puding, Longhai, and Mengding.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again followed Fu Youde in pacifying Wusa and the tribal domains of Qujing, Puding, Longhai, Mengding, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年封永定侯，食祿千五百石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongding with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and hereditary rank as guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongding with a stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and hereditary rank as guard commander.

sentences.zh: 何真，字邦佐，東莞人。

translations.literal: He Zhen, styled Bangzuo, was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen, whose style was Bangzuo, came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 少英偉，好書劍。

translations.literal: In youth he was heroic and imposing and loved books and the sword.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and striking, devoted to both books and the sword.

sentences.zh: 元至正初，為河源縣務副使，轉淡水場管勾，棄官歸。
