translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizheng reign of Yuan he served as deputy commissioner of the Heyuan county office, was transferred to manager of the Danshui salt depot, and then resigned his office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhizheng era he served as deputy commissioner of the Heyuan county magistracy, then as manager of the Danshui salt works, before resigning and returning home.

sentences.zh: 元末盜起，真聚眾保鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan when bandits rose, Zhen gathered followers to protect his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry spread at the end of the Yuan, Zhen raised men to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 十四年，縣人王成、陳仲玉作亂，真赴告元帥府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the county men Wang Cheng and Chen Zhongyu rebelled; Zhen went to report to the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year fellow townsmen Wang Cheng and Chen Zhongyu rose in revolt; Zhen went to the marshal's headquarters to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 帥受賂，反捕真。

translations.literal: The marshal accepted a bribe and instead arrested Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal took a bribe and had Zhen arrested instead.

sentences.zh: 逃居坭岡，舉兵攻成，不克。

translations.literal: Fleeing he took refuge at Nigang, raised troops to attack Cheng, but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Nigang, raised troops against Cheng, but failed to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 久之，惠州人王仲剛與叛將黃常據惠。

translations.literal: After a long time the Huizhou man Wang Zhonggang together with the renegade general Huang Chang held Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Wang Zhonggang of Huizhou and the turncoat general Huang Chang seized Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 真擊走常，殺仲剛。

translations.literal: Zhen drove off Chang and killed Zhonggang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen routed Huang Chang and killed Wang Zhonggang.

sentences.zh: 以功授惠陽路同知、廣東都元帥，守惠州。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed associate administrator of Huiyang Circuit and Grand Marshal of Guangdong, defending Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made associate administrator of Huiyang Circuit and Grand Marshal of Guangdong, with charge of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 海寇邵宗愚陷廣州。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Shao Zongyu captured Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Shao Zongyu seized Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 真以兵破走之，復其城。

translations.literal: Zhen with troops defeated and drove him off and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen drove him off by force and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 擢廣東分省參政，尋擢右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted participating administrator of the Guangdong Branch Secretariat and soon promoted right vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted participating administrator of the Guangdong Branch Secretariat and soon afterward made its right vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 贛州熊天瑞引舟師數萬，欲圖真，真迎之胥江。

translations.literal: Xiong Tianrui of Ganzhou led a fleet of tens of thousands, intending to attack Zhen; Zhen went to meet him on the Xujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tianrui of Ganzhou brought a fleet of tens of thousands to move against Zhen; Zhen met him on the Xujiang.

sentences.zh: 天大雷雨，折天瑞舟檣，擊走之。

translations.literal: Heaven sent great thunder and rain, breaking Tianrui's masts and yards; Zhen struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: A violent thunderstorm snapped Tianrui's masts; Zhen attacked and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 廣人賴以完。

translations.literal: The people of Guang relied on this to remain intact.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong owed their survival to that victory.

sentences.zh: 先是真再攻成，誅仲玉而成卒固守。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhen had twice attacked Cheng, executed Zhongyu, yet Cheng still held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhen had twice attacked Wang Cheng; he had executed Chen Zhongyu, but Cheng continued to hold out.

sentences.zh: 二十六年復圍成，募擒成者，予鈔十千。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again besieged Cheng, offering a reward of ten thousand in paper notes to whoever captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he besieged Cheng again, promising ten thousand in paper notes to whoever brought him in.

sentences.zh: 成奴縛成以出。

translations.literal: Cheng's slave bound Cheng and brought him out.
translations.idiomatic: One of Cheng's slaves bound his master and turned him over.

sentences.zh: 真予之鈔，命具湯鑊，趨烹奴，號於眾曰：「奴叛主者視此！」

translations.literal: Zhen gave him the notes, ordered a cauldron of boiling water prepared, hurried to boil the slave, and cried out to the crowd: "Slaves who betray their masters — look upon this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen paid the reward, had a cauldron of boiling water set up, and had the slave thrown in to die; then he shouted to the crowd, "Let all who see a slave betray his master look upon this!

sentences.zh: 緣海叛者皆降。

translations.literal: All rebels along the coast submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels all along the coast submitted.

sentences.zh: 時中原大亂，嶺表隔絕，有勸真效尉佗故事者，不聽。

translations.literal: At that time the Central Plain was in great chaos and Lingnan was cut off; some urged Zhen to follow the example of Wei Tuo, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: With the Central Plain in turmoil and Lingnan cut off from the north, some urged Zhen to declare himself a regional king as Wei Tuo had done, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 屢遣使由海道貢方物於朝。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys by sea route to present local products to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent envoys by sea to present tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 累進資德大夫、行省左丞。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotion he rose to Grand Master of Virtuous Achievement and left vice administrator of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Grand Master of Virtuous Achievement and left vice administrator of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，太祖命廖永忠為征南將軍，帥舟師取廣東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu the Founding Emperor appointed Liao Yongzhong General Who Conquers the South and ordered him to lead the fleet to take Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu the Founding Emperor appointed Liao Yongzhong General Who Conquers the South and sent him with a fleet to take Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 永忠至福州，以書諭真，遂航海趨潮州。

translations.literal: Yongzhong reached Fuzhou, sent a letter to instruct Zhen, and then sailed toward Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong reached Fuzhou, wrote to Zhen urging submission, and then put to sea for Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 師既至，真遣都事劉克佐詣軍門上印章，籍所部郡縣戶口兵糧，奉表以降。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, Zhen sent chief secretary Liu Kezuo to the camp gate to surrender his seal, register the population, troops, and grain of the prefectures and counties under his command, and submit a memorial of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the army arrived, Zhen sent chief secretary Liu Kezuo to camp to surrender his seal, submit registers of the population, troops, and grain supplies under his command, and offer a memorial of submission.

sentences.zh: 永忠聞於朝，賜詔褒真曰：「朕惟古之豪傑，保境安民，以待有德。

translations.literal: Yongzhong reported to the court, and an edict was bestowed praising Zhen: "I consider that heroes of old kept their borders and settled the people, waiting for one of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong reported to court, and an edict praised Zhen: "I reflect that the heroes of antiquity secured their territories and kept the people at peace, waiting for a ruler of virtue.

sentences.zh: 若竇融、李勣之屬，擁兵據險，角立群雄間，非真主不屈。

translations.literal: Men like Dou Rong and Li Ji held troops and occupied strategic terrain, standing like horns among contending warlords, and would not submit except to the true ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Dou Rong and Li Ji held armies in defensible terrain and stood among rival warlords as equals, bowing only to the true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 此漢、唐名臣，於今未見。

translations.literal: Such famous ministers of Han and Tang have not been seen until now.
translations.idiomatic: Such ministers of Han and Tang fame had not been seen again—until now.

sentences.zh: 爾真連數郡之眾，乃不煩一兵，保境來歸，雖竇、李奚讓焉。」

translations.literal: You, Zhen, holding the multitudes of several prefectures, yet without troubling a single soldier came with your territory to submit — even Dou and Li would yield before this.
translations.idiomatic: You, Zhen, held several prefectures and came in with your territory without a single soldier being sent against you—even Dou Rong and Li Ji would have to yield pride of place.

sentences.zh: 永忠抵東莞，真帥官屬迎勞，遂奉詔入朝。

translations.literal: When Yongzhong reached Dongguan, Zhen led his officials to welcome and entertain him, then followed the edict to enter court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong reached Dongguan; Zhen led his officials out to welcome him, then went to court as the edict directed.

sentences.zh: 擢江西行省參知政事，且諭之曰：「天下分爭，所謂豪傑有三：易亂為治者，上也；

translations.literal: He was promoted participating administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, and moreover was instructed: "When the realm is divided in strife, so-called heroes fall into three kinds: those who turn chaos into order rank highest;
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted participating administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and told: "In a divided realm, heroes fall into three kinds: those who turn chaos into order are the highest;

sentences.zh: 保民達變，知所歸者，次也；

translations.literal: those who preserve the people, grasp change, and know where to turn rank next;
translations.idiomatic: those who protect the people, read the times, and know where their loyalty belongs rank next;

sentences.zh: 負固偷安，身死不悔，斯其下矣。

translations.literal: those who cling stubbornly to ease, die without regret — these are the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: those who cling defiantly to temporary safety and die unrepentant are the lowest of all.

sentences.zh: 卿輸誠納土，不逆顏行，可謂識時務者。」

translations.literal: You offered sincerity and surrendered your land, not turning your face away — this may be called knowing the times.」
translations.idiomatic: You came forward in sincerity and surrendered your territory without hostile defiance — you may truly be called one who knew the times.」

sentences.zh: 真頓首謝。

translations.literal: Zhen bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 在官頗著聲望，尤喜儒術，讀書綴文。

translations.literal: In office he enjoyed considerable reputation, especially loved Confucian learning, and read books and composed prose.
translations.idiomatic: In office he enjoyed a strong reputation, took special delight in Confucian learning, and devoted himself to reading and literary composition.

sentences.zh: 已，轉山東參政。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be associate administrator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as associate administrator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 四年命還廣東，收集舊卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to return to Guangdong to gather former soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered back to Guangdong to gather his former troops.

sentences.zh: 事竣，仍蒞山東。

translations.literal: When the task was finished, he again took up his post in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When the task was complete, he returned to his post in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 九年致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 大軍征雲南，命真偕其子兵馬指揮貴往。

translations.literal: When the main army campaigned against Yunnan, Zhen was ordered to go together with his son Gui, cavalry and infantry commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched against Yunnan, Zhen was ordered to go with his son Gui, who served as cavalry and infantry commander.

sentences.zh: 規畫軍餉，置郵驛。

translations.literal: He planned military provisions and established postal relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: He organized military supplies and established postal relay stations.

sentences.zh: 遷山西右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right administration commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 再與貴勾軍廣東，擢貴鎮南衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Again together with Gui he mustered troops in Guangdong; Gui was promoted to vice commander of the Zhennan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He again mustered troops in Guangdong with Gui, who was promoted to vice commander of the Zhennan Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋命真為浙江布政使，改湖廣。

translations.literal: Soon Zhen was appointed administration commissioner of Zhejiang, then transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was soon appointed administration commissioner of Zhejiang, then transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 二十年復致仕，封東莞伯，祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he retired again, was enfeoffed as Earl of Dongguan with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he retired once more, was enfeoffed as Earl of Dongguan with an income of fifteen hundred shi of grain, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子榮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 與弟貴及尚寶司丞宏皆坐藍黨死。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Gui and Vice Director of the Imperial Seal Office Hong, he was executed for association with Lan Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He, his younger brother Gui, and Vice Director of the Imperial Seal Office Hong were all executed for association with Lan Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 真弟迪疑禍及己，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Di, fearing disaster would reach him, then raised a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Di, fearing he would be implicated, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 擊殺南海官軍三百余人，遁入海島。

translations.literal: He attacked and killed more than three hundred Nanhai government troops and fled to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: He killed more than three hundred government troops in Nanhai and fled to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 廣東都司發兵討擒之，伏誅。

translations.literal: The Guangdong regional command dispatched troops to suppress and capture him; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong regional command sent troops to capture him, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：陳友諒之克太平也，其鋒甚銳，微茂才則金陵之安危未可知矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Chen Youliang captured Taiping, his momentum was very sharp; but for Maocai, the safety or peril of Jinling would have been unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When Chen Youliang captured Taiping, his momentum was fierce; but for Kang Maocai, the fate of Jinling might well have hung in the balance.

sentences.zh: 吳良守江陰，耿炳文守長興，而吳人不得肆其志。

translations.literal: Wu Liang garrisoned Jiangyin and Geng Bingwen garrisoned Changxing, and the men of Wu could not carry out their designs.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu Liang holding Jiangyin and Geng Bingwen holding Changxing, the Wu forces could not achieve their aims.

sentences.zh: 締造之基，其力為多。

translations.literal: In laying the foundation of the dynasty, their contribution was great.
translations.idiomatic: In laying the foundations of the dynasty, their contribution was immense.

sentences.zh: 至若華雲龍、張赫、吳復、胡海之屬，或威著邊疆，或功存海運，搴旗陷陣，所向皆摧。

translations.literal: As for men such as Hua Yunlong, Zhang He, Wu Fu, and Hu Hai, some won fame on the frontier, others preserved merit in maritime transport; seizing banners and breaking battle lines, wherever they went all was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: As for men such as Hua Yunlong, Zhang He, Wu Fu, and Hu Hai, some won renown on the frontier, others distinguished themselves in maritime transport; seizing enemy banners and breaking through battle lines, they swept aside all who stood before them.

sentences.zh: 揆之前代功臣，何多讓焉。

translations.literal: Measured against meritorious ministers of earlier dynasties, how much would they yield?
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the great ministers of earlier dynasties, they would yield little.

sentences.zh: 而又皆能保守祿位，以恩禮令終，斯其尤足嘉美者歟！

translations.literal: Moreover, all were able to preserve their stipends and ranks and end their lives in imperial favor and courtesy — is this not especially worthy of praise!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they were able to preserve their ranks and stipends and end their lives in honor and imperial favor — is this not especially worthy of praise!
